bridging_prereqs.why_needed: 6-Ⅴ-3 assumes these steps. Most 國寫 0-score papers are blank or not full sentences, and 審題 errors cost points.

common_misconceptions.misconception: 國綜 only tests the textbook selections, so memorizing the 課文 is enough.
common_misconceptions.correct_idea: CEEC deliberately sets no fixed textbook share. Source texts span classical, modern, and cross-disciplinary material, and unseen texts are paired with 課內 ones.

common_misconceptions.misconception: 選修「國學常識」 is part of the 學測, so 國學常識 must be memorized broadly.
common_misconceptions.correct_idea: 加深加廣選修 (including 國學常識) is excluded from 國綜. Literary and cultural knowledge within 必修 (A5/A6) can still appear, as in 115 Q28.

common_misconceptions.misconception: 混合題 short answers are like mini 國寫 essays, so personal opinions earn points.
common_misconceptions.correct_idea: 混合題 answers are convergent and text-based. They are scored on key ideas (full, partial, or zero), and copying, vagueness, or a missing required dimension loses points.

common_misconceptions.misconception: In 國寫 Q1(一) it is fine to copy sentences from the given passage.
common_misconceptions.correct_idea: Answers that only copy the passage are capped. In 113, copying alone earned at most 1 point per side, and copying the prompt scores 0. Paraphrase in your own words.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A well-written but unfinished 國寫 essay can still score A.
common_misconceptions.correct_idea: An unfinished essay is capped at B+ (14 for Q1(二), 17 for Q2), as is a single-paragraph Q2 essay.

common_misconceptions.misconception: In 115 國寫 Q1, 「臉」 means the animal's physical face.
common_misconceptions.correct_idea: The passage uses Levinas's ethical 「臉」. Answers equating it with a physical face were judged not fully correct.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Because 學測 questions are not copyrightable, any passage inside them can be reposted freely.
common_misconceptions.correct_idea: TIPO's committee held that a work used inside an exam question stays protected on its own; only the question as a whole is unprotected. Answers and explanations may also be protected.

recent_trends.trend: Non-choice share of 國綜 settled at 20 points. It was 18 in 111 and 112 (three items each) and 20 in 113, 114, and 115 (three items, sub-parts of 2 or 4 points).

混合題 has become a large thematic 題組 built on several texts. 113 used four texts on memory, mixing literature, neuroscience, and 李煜/辛棄疾 詞. 115 used three texts under 「聽見她的聲音」 (歸有光, a modern essay, oral history). 114 built a concept-framework dialogue on 〈虯髯客傳〉 and 《西遊記》.

The 15篇 recommended classical texts anchor many items through 對讀 and 字義 comparisons. In 115, items Q1, 2, 4, 14–15, 25, 28, 30–36 drew on them. 114 used the most direct textbook-selection material in four years, about 30 points.

Reading dominates. Teachers put 113 at about 80% reading, and 115 at about 80% passage reading and technique versus about 20% basic items. Inference and source-evaluation items increased in 115 (e.g., Q4, 7, 12, 36; and Q22–24 comparing commentaries on a 杜甫 poem).

Cross-disciplinary popular-science and academic texts appear every year: climate change (111); national defense, astronomy, medicine (112); brain and memory (113); 擬社會互動 in 國寫 (114); 臺灣杉 phylogeography, soap chemistry, calligraphy, music (115).
Taiwan material is prominent: 洪繻〈籌海議〉 (112), 臺灣杉 and an oral history of a Taiwanese grandmother (115), and 鄭用錫/林占梅 congratulatory poems (115).
Basic-knowledge item types come and go. 113 had no 國學常識 or 應用文. 115 brought back 文法 (量詞, presented as a table) and 國學常識 (韻文). 新詩 was absent in 115.

The 國寫 Q1 structure is stable: about 80字 for 4 pts plus about 400字 for 21 pts, on a social phenomenon (Holmes/Watson 112, 標籤 113, 擬社會互動 114, ethical responsibility and the 「臉」 115). Q2 is a 25-point affective essay prompted by images, science, or poetry (52赫茲 114, 幾米 picture-texts 115). A-grade shares stay low (about 6–15%) and B dominates (about 71–81%).

pedagogy_notes: Copyright, classical texts: works by long-dead authors (e.g., the 15篇) are far beyond the 著作權法 §30 term of life plus 50 years. Punctuated or annotated modern editions, 語譯, and textbook 注釋 may carry their own protection. Prefer our own transcription with our own notes. If reusing 維基文庫 transcriptions, follow CC BY-SA 4.0: attribute and share alike.

Copyright, modern 白話文 (most textbook modern selections, e.g., 琦君〈髻〉 cited in 113): check each author's death year against §30 before quoting more than briefly. A free website is not a school (§46) or a 審定 textbook (§47), so rely on §52 合理引用 plus §65 fair-use factors and always cite (§64). In practice: write our own summaries and analysis, quote only short excerpts that are necessary for the teaching point, and link to legitimate full texts. Do not reproduce whole works.

Copyright, past 學測 papers: link to CEEC's official PDFs rather than rehosting. §9(1)(5) may exempt the questions, but TIPO's 93年 committee held that passages inside questions stay protected when used separately. Answers and explanations may be protected (TIPO 1111221). CEEC claims copyright on its 考試說明, slides, and 選才電子報 and limits use to non-profit with attribution, with no large-scale copying without consent. Practice items should be original ones written in CEEC's formats.

MOE dictionaries (重編國語辭典修訂本, 簡編本, 國語小字典, 成語典) are CC BY-ND 3.0 TW and allow commercial use. We may display entries verbatim with the required attribution (教育部, dictionary name, version number, URL). We may not edit entries or convert them to 簡化字. 異體字字典 is 'All rights reserved', so link only. For ctext.org, link only, because its site says scraping violates its ToS.

Sequence like the 課綱 spiral (◎ items recur across stages). Do bridging units first (注音 → 部首/部件 → 標點 → 句型 → 4 造字原則 → 國中 文言 basics Ab-Ⅳ-6/7). Then go to Ab-Ⅴ, Ac-Ⅴ, Ad-Ⅴ, then text types B, then culture C. Interleave each 15篇 lesson right after the genre or text-type unit it exemplifies (e.g., 赤壁賦 after Ad-Ⅴ-3 辭賦, 諫逐客書 and 師說 after Bd-Ⅴ argument). Avoid introducing a genre term before its unit.
Mirror the official 文言 ramp. 國中 rises from 10–20% to 25–35%, and 高中 averages 35–45%. A beginner track should grow 文言 exposure gradually instead of starting with 先秦 texts.

Weight practice like the exam. About 80% of 國綜 is passage reading, much of it multi-text 對讀, and about 20% basic knowledge. Design lessons around reading levels (擷取檢索 → 統整解釋 → 反思評價) rather than memorization.

混合題 answer craft, from the CEEC 評分原則 articles: answer every requested dimension, use key terms precisely and correctly (錯別字 on key terms are deducted), paraphrase rather than copy, and stay within suggested length.

國寫 craft, from CEEC: 審題 the key concepts, include every element the prompt requires (e.g., 事例 + 立場 + 省思), finish the essay, use paragraphs, write inside the answer area, use 正體中文 only, and check punctuation. The unofficial 三項心法 (精準審題, 扣題發揮, 真情表達) from a teacher in 聯合報 is consistent with this but is secondary.

Professor–student dialogue (OSTEP-style) fits 國文 well for modeling 審題, inference chains, and why a distractor is wrong. Label dialogues as teaching scaffolds and keep every factual statement inside them sourced.

Visualizations that map directly onto official structures: a 學習內容 code tree (A/B/C → Aa…Cc); a 15篇 timeline (先秦 → 漢魏六朝 → 唐宋 → 明清 → 臺灣古典散文); a genre map for 韻文 and 非韻文 (Ad-Ⅴ-3/4); a rubric chart for 三等六級 bands; and stacked bars of 國寫 A/B/C distributions for 111–115.

For English readers: show 正體 characters with 注音 and add English glosses. Explain that 國寫 must be written in 正體中文. Keep zh-TW terms visible beside English because CEEC and 課綱 terms have no official English names (CEEC's English page is outdated).

Beta caveat for the Chinese track: the A/B/C 類 textbook-selection lists, the 中華文化基本教材 selections, and grade placement of the 15篇 vary by publisher and were not verified. Present them as 'check your textbook version'.

open_questions: No 116-specific 國文 考試說明 was found. The 108年9月 guide (111學年度起適用) plus the 116 簡章 appear to govern, but I did not confirm that CEEC issued no newer 國文 guidance for 116.

CEEC's own per-year 國綜 試題分析 (official distribution of items across A1–B5, official 文白 ratio) was not found publicly. It may exist only in the paid 「試題與解析」 books, or the CEEC-hosted 試題研討會 materials. The trend data for 111–114 here rests on 評分原則 articles plus media and teacher reports.
Teacher sources disagree on the 115 國綜 文白 ratio: about 1:1 in the Taipei teachers' report versus 4:6 attributed to a 建中 teacher in news coverage.
The 111 and 112 non-choice totals (18 points) sit below the 20–28 range in the 考試說明 FAQ. CEEC's 111 briefing said 'about 20'. Whether CEEC formally revised the range is unverified.
Which textbook selections are A, B, or C 類 for the 116 cohort, and the current number of 審定 國文 textbook versions (the guide said 5 at the time), were not verified.
The 中華文化基本教材 selections (e.g., 論語/孟子 choices) are not listed in the 課綱 document opened. The 普通型高中 國語文 課程手冊 or textbooks need checking.
Whether any 國語文 課綱 revision after 107年1月 changed the 15篇 list or Stage Ⅴ codes was not verified.
Whether the 學測 legally counts as 「依法令舉行之考試」 under 著作權法 §9(1)(5) is uncertain. TIPO defers to 教育部, and CEEC asserts copyright over its own documents.

I could not verify 樂詞網 reuse terms (the open-data page returned 502) or its official English terms (search results were not retrievable by fetch). All English renderings except GSAT, AST, and CEEC are therefore proposed, not verified.
ctext.org reuse terms are unverified (only an anti-scraping notice was returned).
The 課綱 publishes no official list of 文言 虛字. If the course teaches a core 虛字 list, it needs an authoritative source, such as MOE dictionary entries for each character.
Grade placement (10 / 11 / 12) of each 15篇 text depends on the publisher and was not verified.
Word limits for 國寫 第二大題 in 113–115 were not stated in the summaries I read. The original 試卷 should be checked.
The 115 國寫 佳作 and their official comments were seen only through a secondary report (大學問). The CEEC originals were not opened.
Per-author copyright status (death year + 50) for frequently tested modern authors was not researched and must be checked case by case before quoting.
The WebSearch budget was exhausted during this task, so a few lookups (official English names, 中華文化基本教材 content, 國語文學科中心 resources) could not be done. A follow-up run could complete them.

verification.subject: 國語文 Chinese (beta): 學測國文考科 = 國語文綜合能力測驗（國綜）+ 國語文寫作能力測驗（國寫）, 116學年度
verification.corrected_scope_summary:
Target sitting: 116學年度學科能力測驗, 116年1月22日（五）至24日（日） (Jan 22–24, 2027). Registration ran 115/10/27–11/10. Both 國文 sessions are on 1/23 (Sat): 國文（一）國綜 12:50–14:20 and 國文（二）國寫 15:20–16:50, 90 minutes each (CEEC press release 115.10.23; 116簡章, 初版 115年8月4日).

Scope (116簡章): 國文 = 「必修國文」, 課綱依據 108課綱. 國綜 (out of 100) and 國寫 (out of 50) each count 50%; 國文原得總分 = 國綜×0.5 + 國寫. Scores are 15 級分; the 級距 is the top-1% mean divided by 15. When the 學測 is used for 分發入學, a 60-級分 scale applies.

Governing guide: 學測國文考科考試說明（111學年度起適用, 中華民國108年9月）. 簡章附錄十 says the 111-起 考試說明 set was 「113年07月29日更新」. The 國文 PDF still carries the 108年9月 date; whether its content changed was not verified.

Curriculum basis: 國語文課綱 (中華民國107年1月; the CEEC guide says 教育部 issued it 107年1月25日).
- 學習內容 has three 主題: A 文字篇章 (Aa/Ab/Ac/Ad), B 文本表述 (Ba–Be), C 文化內涵 (Ca/Cb/Cc).
- Stage Ⅴ (grades 10–12) has no Aa items and only one Ac item (Ac-Ⅴ-1).
- 學習表現 has six categories; Stage Ⅴ has none in category 3.
- 普通型高中 必修 is 20學分 (16學分 in grades 10–11 + 4學分 in grade 12), including 中華文化基本教材 2學分. Earlier reporting of "16學分 total" was wrong.
- 加深加廣選修 is 8學分 offered, students take at least 4. Its courses (語文表達與傳播應用、各類文學選讀、專題閱讀與研究、國學常識) are outside the 國綜 scope (guide Q8).
- Required textbooks: 文言 averages 35–45% of lessons over three years, excluding 中華文化基本教材. Each volume has one 文化經典 lesson. Each year has at least one modern and one classical poetry lesson. 附錄四 lists 15 recommended 文言 texts.
- 國綜 文言 sampling 「參酌」 (takes account of) the 35–45% ratio.
- Textbook-selection questions are capped by how many publishers carry the text: B類 ≤40%, C類 ≤10% of textbook-based points; A類 is uncapped.

國綜 objectives:
- A1–A6, knowledge: 字形字音字義, 語詞成語, 語法, 表現手法表述方式, 文學作家作品體類流派, 學術思想文化.
- B1–B5, reading: 檢索擷取, 理解比較分析統整, 延伸反思, 形式推究, 結合文學文化知識的詮釋鑑賞.
- Question types are 單選, 多選, and 混合題.
- The guide plans 20–28 non-choice points. Actual totals: 18 in 111–112 and 20 in 113–115.

國寫: two 大題, 知性的統整判斷 and 情意的感受抒發, graded 三等六級. The question format is officially not fixed. In 111–115, Q1 was split into roughly 4 + 21 points and Q2 was a single 25-point essay. Answers must be in 正體中文 (專有名詞 and special prompts excepted).

Recent 國綜 papers (113–115, per media and teacher reports) are reading-dominated, about 80%. 文白 is about 1:1. Multi-text 混合題 often anchor on the 15篇.

A beginner needs 國小/國中 bridging (課綱 Stage Ⅰ–Ⅳ codes) before Stage Ⅴ units.
verification.exam_format_verified:
Verified against the CEEC press release 115.10.23, 116簡章 (初版 115.08.04), and the 考試說明 (108年9月).

**Schedule (116)**
- Exam runs 116/1/22–24.
- 1/23 (Sat): 國文（一）國綜 12:50–14:20, then 國文（二）國寫 15:20–16:50. Each session is 90 minutes.
- Other subjects: 英文, 數學A, 數學B 100 minutes each; 社會, 自然 110 minutes each.

**Scoring**
- 國綜 is out of 100 and 國寫 out of 50, each worth 50%.
- 國文原得總分 = 國綜得分×0.5 + 國寫得分.
- Max 15 級分. 級距 = mean 原得總分 of the top 1% of examinees ÷ 15.
- When used for 分發入學 the scale is 60 級分.
- A rule violation in either 國文 session deducts from the combined 國文 級分.
- 國寫 also gets its own 成績通知單 with A/B/C 表現描述. Universities may use it in 個人申請.

**國綜 question types**
- Types are 單選, 多選, and 混合題 (a 題組 mixing choice and non-choice items).
- 多選 scoring: (n−2k)/n of the item's points, where k = number of wrong options, floored at 0.
- The guide plans 20–28 non-choice points (10–14% of 國文).
- Actual non-choice points (選才電子報):
  - 111: 18 (Q34–36, 2+4 each)
  - 112: 18 (Q33, 35, 37)
  - 113: 20 (Q32, 33, 36)
  - 114: 20 (Q34–36)
  - 115: 20 (Q32–34; sub-items scored 2/0 or 4/2/0)
- The 111 CEEC briefing said: non-choice about 20 points, 2–3 混合題 sets, more than 30 items.
  - 110 試辦 paper: 25 單選 (7 題組) + 7 多選 = 78 points; 2 混合題 sets = 22 points (18 non-choice); 39 items in total.
- 115 paper (Taipei teachers' report): 24 單選 (48 points), 7 多選 (28), 混合題 choice ×2 (4), short answer ×3 (20); 36 items, 100 points.
- Texts may include 圖表, 圖形, 圖解, 表單 (guide Q2).

**國寫**
- All non-choice, two 大題: 知性的統整判斷 and 情意的感受抒發.
- The format is not fixed (guide Q6: one, two, or even four sub-questions). The guide's own 情意 examples split 7 + 18.
- In 111–115, 第一大題 was (一) about 80字 or 5 lines for 4 points, plus (二) about 400字 or 21 lines for 21 points. 第二大題 was a single 25-point essay.
- Graders decide 等, then 級, then the score.
  - 25-point scale: A+ 25–22, A 21–18, B+ 17–14, B 13–10, C+ 9–6, C 5–1, 0.
  - (一): A 4–3, B 2, C 1, 0.
  - (二) on 21 points: A+ 21–19, A 18–15, B+ 14–12, B 11–8, C+ 7–5, C 4–1.
- Recurring special rules (they vary by year and question):
  - Blank, off-topic, or copying the prompt scores 0.
  - Writing outside the answer area costs 1 point.
  - Punctuation and 錯別字 are deducted at the grader's discretion.
  - An unfinished essay, or a Q2 written as one paragraph, is capped at B+.
  - Self-titled Q2 essays: capped at B+ 17 in 111 and 113; no deduction in 114 and 115.
- Prompt-writing rules: quoted material is preferably 800字 or less, avoids obscure jargon, needs no specialist knowledge, and word limits are set per question.
- Answers must be in 正體中文, except 專有名詞 or where the prompt says otherwise (簡章附錄三).

corrections.original: 普通型高中 time allocation is 必修 16學分, which includes 中華文化基本教材 2學分 (also unit 21: 屬於必修16學分中的2學分).
corrections.correction: The 課綱 時間分配 table lists 必修 as 16學分 for grades 10–11 plus 4學分 for grade 12, which is 20學分 in total. 備註1 says 必修 includes 中華文化基本教材 2學分. 加深加廣選修 is 8學分 across grades 10–12, with students taking at least 4.
corrections.source_url: https://www.naer.edu.tw/upload/1/16/doc/806/十二年國民基本教育課程綱要國民中小學暨普通型高級中等學校語文領域-國語文.odt

corrections.original: The governing CEEC exam guide is 學測國文考科考試說明（111學年度起適用, 108年9月）; I found no 116-specific revision.
corrections.correction: The guide opened is still dated 108年9月. However, 116簡章 附錄十 describes the 「111學年度起適用之大學入學考試『考試說明』」 as 「113年07月29日更新」. Whether that update changed the 國文 guide was not verified, so the course should re-check the CEEC 考試說明 page.

corrections.original: 國綜 文言 sampling follows that ratio (35–45%).
corrections.correction: The guide says only that the 國綜 文言 sampling ratio 「參酌此原則」, meaning it takes the 課綱 35–45% textbook rule into account. It is not a fixed exam quota.

corrections.original: Answers must be in 正體中文.
corrections.correction: 簡章附錄三: 「限用正體中文書寫，惟專有名詞或試題有特殊要求者不在此限」. So 專有名詞 and prompts with special requirements are exempt.

corrections.original: 國寫 第一大題 split (一) about 80字 for 4 pts and (二) about 400字 for 21 pts; 第二大題 25 pts (presented as the format).
corrections.correction: This is the pattern actually used in 111–115, not a rule. Guide Q6 says 國寫's question form is not fixed: one 大題, two 小題, or even four. The guide's own 情意 examples split 7 + 18 points.

corrections.original: 112 國綜: the other set links 《獅子王》 and 《哈姆雷特》 with Adam Grant's 《反叛,改變世界的力量》 (Originals).
corrections.correction: CEEC's article says Q37's text was adapted from 亞當‧格蘭特《作個原創者》 (tr. 黃翫); the title 《反叛…》 does not appear. CEEC also lists Q35's text as 明代許潮《赤壁遊》 雜劇, an extension of 〈赤壁賦〉. The 18 non-choice points (Q33, 35, 37, 6 each) are confirmed.

corrections.original: 115: Q1–2 and Q14–15 draw on 〈虯髯客傳〉〈項脊軒志〉〈勸和論〉; Q32–36 use 〈項脊軒志〉.
corrections.correction:
Per the teachers' report:
- Q1 (字音) options come from 〈虬髯客傳〉〈先妣事略〉〈項脊軒志〉〈勸和論〉.
- Q2 (字形) tests common miswritten words and does not come from the 15篇.
- Q14 draws on 〈勸和論〉〈馮諼客孟嘗君〉〈劉姥姥〉〈虬髯客傳〉.
- Q15 is unattributed 白話.
- 甲 (歸有光's three texts) is used in Q32, 35 and 36. Q33–34 use 乙 (李欣倫〈水面下〉) and 丙 (an interview with 曾林阿珠).

corrections.original: Unit 勸和論: 115第2題字形、第14–15題量詞; Unit 虯髯客傳: 115第1、14–15、25題.
corrections.correction: 勸和論: 115 Q1 (字音, option D) and Q14 (量詞). 虯髯客傳: 115 Q1, Q14 and Q25. Neither text is used in Q2 or Q15.

corrections.original: 115 國綜 混合題: 乙 is a modern essay on parenting, 丙 is an oral-history interview with a 媳婦仔.
corrections.correction: 乙 is 李欣倫〈水面下〉; CEEC's article does not name the author. 丙 is adapted from 張秋美's interview 《消失中的台灣阿嬤‧將女兒送養的阿母——曾林阿珠》 (the report also writes the name as 曾秋美). The interviewee is a mother who gave up a daughter for adoption. CEEC describes the interview as being about her 六女兒's match with her 養兄.

corrections.original: Unit 文學常識 in_gsat = partial.
corrections.correction: A5 (文學作家、作品、體類、流派) and A6 are explicit 國綜 測驗目標, and 命題重點（二） covers them. Only the elective course 國學常識 is excluded, so in_gsat should be yes.

corrections.original: Unit 加深加廣選修 grade_level 11–12 選修.
corrections.correction: The 課綱 時間分配 table places the 8學分 加深加廣選修 across grades 10–12 (a three-column span). Schools decide the actual grade.

confirmed_facts.claim: 116學測 is 116年1月22日（五）–24日（日）. Registration runs 115/10/27–11/10. The six subjects are 國文, 英文, 數學A, 數學B, 社會 and 自然. 國文 is split into 國綜 and 國寫 sessions.

On 1/23 (Sat), 國綜 runs 12:50–14:20 and 國寫 15:20–16:50, 90 minutes each. All subjects except 國寫 have choice items, and every subject has non-choice or 混合題 items. Scores are reported as 級分, max 15. 級距 = top-1% mean ÷ 15. When used for 分發入學 the scale is 60 級分.
116簡章 (初版 115年8月4日): the 國文 scope is 必修國文 and the 課綱 basis is 108課綱. 國綜 is out of 100 and 國寫 out of 50, each worth 50%. 國文原得總分 = 國綜×0.5 + 國寫. 附錄三 gives the 國寫 表現描述 (A/B/C/0) and the 正體中文 rule.
The 考試說明 is titled 「學科能力測驗國文考科考試說明－111學年度起適用」 and dated 中華民國108年9月. Its 前言 says the exam is based on the 國語文課綱's 普通型高中 部定必修 courses. Footnote 1 says the 課綱 was issued by 教育部 on 107年1月25日.
國綜 objectives A1–A6 and B1–B5 match the report's wording. The guide's 命題重點 are (一) 字詞語法, (二) 文學知識, (三) 文本涵義, (四) 寫作方式手法 and (五) 文化內涵.

取材原則: textbook selections are classed A (4–5 versions), B (2–3) or C (1). C類 is capped at 10% and B類 at 40% of textbook-based points; A類 is uncapped. At the time there were 5 審定 versions, so for example 30 points allow ≤12 from B類 and ≤3 from C類.

Guide FAQ: 「文本」 includes 圖表, 圖形, 圖解 and 表單 (Q2). Non-choice items are planned at 20–28 of 100 points, i.e. 10–14% of 國文 (Q5). No fixed share comes from textbook selections (Q6). The four 加深加廣 electives are excluded (Q8).

國寫: both objectives are as described in the report. The three-tier, six-band (三等六級) scale is A+ 25–22, A 21–18, B+ 17–14, B 13–10, C+ 9–6, C 5–1, 0. Graders decide 等, then 級, then the score. Prompt rules: quoted material ≤800字, no obscure jargon, no specialist knowledge required. A separate 國寫 成績通知單 with 表現描述 may be used in 個人申請.

CEEC's 111學測簡介─國文考科 (民國110年11月) says 國綜 non-choice is about 20 points, with 單選, 多選 and 2–3 混合題 sets, more than 30 items. The 110 試辦 paper had 單選25 (7 題組) + 多選7 = 78 points, plus 2 混合題 sets = 22 points (18 non-choice), 39 items in total. CEEC's stated principles: 依據課綱命題、不超綱不偏本, 兼顧基本題, and text volume similar to recent years.

The 國語文課綱 cover is dated 中華民國一○七年一月. 學習內容 has three 主題: 文字篇章 (Aa, Ab, Ac, Ad), 文本表述 (Ba–Be) and 文化內涵 (Ca, Cb, Cc). Codes read 主題項目-學習階段-流水號, where Ⅴ = grades 10–12, and ◎ marks content repeated across stages. Every Stage Ⅴ code in the report's units exists with the stated wording.

verification.notes:
**Method**
- WebSearch was used up after its first call (the session-wide limit), so all checks were done by fetching the cited primary documents directly, plus my own reading of the downloaded PDFs and the NAER ODT. Nothing was written to the project.
- Fully checked:
  - CEEC press release 115.10.23
  - 116簡章, all 79 pages
  - 學測國文考試說明 (108年9月), all 58 pages
  - 國語文課綱 ODT: full text and the time-allocation table cells
  - All ten 選才電子報 articles for 111–115
  - 111學測簡介 slides
  - Taipei teachers' 115 report
  - 著作權法, the two TIPO documents, the MOE license, and the news items

**Main errors found**
1. 必修國文 is 20學分 (16 in grades 10–11 + 4 in grade 12, including 中華文化基本教材 2學分), not 16.
2. Several 115 item-to-text attributions were wrong (Q2, Q15; 混合題 甲 used only in Q32/35/36).
3. The 112 Adam Grant book title differs from CEEC's citation (《作個原創者》).
4. The 國寫 format is officially not fixed; the 4+21 / 25 split is only the 111–115 pattern.
5. 簡章 附錄十 shows a 113.07.29 update to the 考試說明 set, which the report missed.

**Structural notes for the course plan**
- Stage Ⅴ has only one Ac code and no Aa code, so grammar and 語詞/成語 units must cite Stage Ⅱ–Ⅳ codes. Label these as earlier-stage foundations.
- The 課綱 does not map the 15篇 to 學習內容 codes. Present any mapping as the course's own teaching design.
- One unit was added: 文化經典選文與先秦諸子. The 課綱 requires one 文化經典 lesson per volume, and the guide's A6 explanation names the 諸子 texts.
- final_units keep all 15篇 after the genre, text-type and culture units, so every depends_on points to an earlier unit. If you prefer to interleave each text right after its genre unit, the dependencies still hold.
- 學習表現 categories 1 (聆聽) and 2 (口語表達) are in the 課綱 but are not tested on the paper 學測. Treat them as optional enrichment.

research.topic: Learning design for a zero-to-hero, dialogue-based, bilingual (EN / zh-TW) 學測 (GSAT) course website: OSTEP dialogue format, evidence for dialogue learning, evidence-based techniques, prerequisite mapping, bilingual UX, and an exam-prep layer

findings.area: 1a. OSTEP dialogue format: where, how often, how long, what they do
findings.recommendation: Use Professor–Student dialogues as short interludes, not as the whole text. (1) Open each major unit with a dialogue that sets up the big idea through one concrete everyday analogy and names the unit's few key ideas. (2) Close each unit with a 'summary dialogue': the Student recaps and the Professor probes. Turn this into retrieval practice by asking the reader to answer the Professor's recap question before showing the Student's answer. (3) Teach the main lessons in structured prose with figures, using OSTEP-style devices: an explicit 'crux of the problem' question at the top, behavior-over-time timelines and diagrams, clearly marked asides and tips, and practice generators with self-check. Aim for about 1–4 printed pages per dialogue. Order units so a problem's prerequisites come before the problem.
findings.rationale: OSTEP's preface says the dialogue is used to introduce the major thematic concepts and to review material from time to time, and also as a chance for humor. The table of contents puts a 'Dialogue' at the start of each part (ch. 1 book, 3 virtualization, 12 memory virtualization, 25 concurrency, 35 persistence, 52 security, plus VMM, monitors, distribution and labs) and 'Summary' dialogues at the end of parts (ch. 11 CPU, 24 VM, 34 threads, 46 files, 51 distribution). The three dialogues opened here are each about 2 pages. The virtualization dialogue introduces the concept with a 'physical vs. virtual peach' analogy and then moves to the CPU. The CPU summary dialogue has the Student list the mechanisms learned while the Professor probes the deeper philosophy. The preface also describes the other devices: the crux of the problem, timelines, asides/tips, and homework simulators that take a random seed to generate a 'virtually infinite set of problems' and can solve them for self-checking. On sequencing, the 'To Educators' section says concurrency is deliberately placed after CPU and memory virtualization, because students struggle to see why the concurrency problem arises without those prerequisites.
findings.license_or_terms: Format idea only; see 1b for license.

findings.area: 1b. OSTEP: the authors' stated rationale and inspiration, and the license
findings.recommendation: Borrow only the idea of the format: generic roles named 'Professor' and 'Student', and interlude placement. Write every line of dialogue and every analogy from scratch. Do not reuse OSTEP text, its peach analogy, or its jokes. Credit OSTEP as format inspiration on an About page, linking to ostep.org rather than hosting copies. Keep a single consistent authorial voice across both languages; the authors cite this as a reason the book is not open source.
findings.rationale: The preface calls the dialogue 'one of the oldest didactic methods'. It names no specific model for the dialogue form. The title is an homage to Feynman's lecture notes (Six Easy Pieces), but that is about the title, not the dialogues. In Dialogue 1 the Professor explains that the dialogues are moments to step outside the narrative and think. A preface footnote says 'free' does not mean open source and that the book is copyrighted with the usual protections. The authors wanted one voice and say the book should feel like a dialogue with the person explaining. The website says the book will always be free in PDF form and asks people to link to the chapters rather than make local copies. The preface footer reads '© 2008–26, Arpaci-Dusseau' and 'Version 1.20', while the website lists Version 1.10 (Nov 2023).
findings.license_or_terms: © Arpaci-Dusseau. Free to read online but explicitly not open source; usual copyright protections apply. The authors ask readers to link rather than make local copies. No text reuse.

findings.area: 2a. Evidence on learning from observed dialogue (vicarious learning; Chi et al.; Muller et al.)
findings.recommendation: Write dialogues where the Student is a genuine novice. The Student asks the beginner questions, says 'what does that word mean?', and sometimes makes realistic, documented errors that the Professor then corrects (a 'conflict episode'). At each such point, make the reader do the same task the Student faces: a required pause-and-answer input box before the Professor's reply, then feedback. Never let the dialogue be read passively from start to finish. Prefer the Student solving a step over the Professor lecturing at length.
findings.rationale:
Chi, Roy & Hausmann (2008, Cognitive Science 32(2):301–341): pairs of students who collaboratively watched videos of another student being tutored learned physics problem-solving about as well as the tutees. Tutoring helped when students constructed knowledge themselves or jointly with the tutor, not when the tutor only transmitted it.

Chi, Kang & Yaghmourian (2017, J. Learning Sciences 26:10–50), two studies: college students learned more from tutorial dialogue-videos than from lecture-style monologue-videos covering the same content (average lengths about 25 vs 21 min, not significantly different). On 11 deep transfer items, dialogue-observers gained significantly (d = 1.08) and did not differ from the tutees; monologue-observers' gain was not significant. Dialogue-observers worked their workbook problems themselves rather than copying them (16.7 vs 5.3 of 22). They referred to and elaborated on what the tutee said more than on what the tutor said, and produced more substantive comments right after tutee errors. The tutor and tutee moves themselves did not correlate with observers' learning. The authors attribute the advantage to the observers' own constructive and interactive engagement (the ICAP framework). They also note that observers did the same worksheets as the tutee.

Muller, Sharma, Eklund & Reimann (2007, Instructional Science 35(6):519–533): a student–tutor dialogue video built around common alternative conceptions outperformed an expository video on quantum tunneling (d = 0.71).

Muller, Bewes, Sharma & Reimann (2008, JCAL; n = 364, Newton's laws): Refutation (0.79) and Dialogue (0.83) gave the largest gains over Exposition, and low-prior-knowledge students benefited most.

Caveats: these studies used college students, mostly lab settings, small samples, and pairs of observers with worksheets.
findings.license_or_terms: Cite the papers. Do not reproduce their transcripts.

findings.area: 2b. Conversational style / Mayer's personalization principle
findings.recommendation: Write in a conversational, second-person, polite register in both English and zh-TW (address the reader directly with 'you' / 你). Keep each lesson chunk short: well under about 35 minutes of study. Split long topics into several short lessons, each with its own checks.
findings.rationale: Ginns, Martin & Marsh (2013, Educational Psychology Review 25(4):445–472) meta-analysis of conversational vs formal instructional text: retention d = 0.30, transfer d = 0.54, perceived friendliness d = 0.46. Instructional time was the clearest boundary condition: effects were small and non-significant in lessons longer than 35 minutes.

findings.area: 3a. Retrieval practice (testing effect)
findings.recommendation: Make recall the main review action, not rereading. (1) In-dialogue 'Your turn' prompts: the reader must type or choose an answer before the reveal. (2) End-of-lesson checks with 3–6 short-answer or free-recall items and feedback after each attempt. (3) A flashcard-style review where the learner produces the answer first, then checks it; repeat until the item is recalled correctly once, then reschedule it for another day. Do not build headline features around highlighting or rereading. Add a short note to learners explaining that rereading feels more effective than it is.
findings.rationale: Roediger & Karpicke (2006, Psychological Science 17(3):249–255): at 5 minutes restudying beat testing, but at 2 days and 1 week prior testing gave much better retention. Restudying made students more confident without the matching retention. Dunlosky et al. (2013, PSPI 14(1):4–58), per Dunlosky's 2013 American Educator article: practice testing and distributed practice rated most effective; interleaving, elaborative interrogation and self-explanation 'promising'; rereading, highlighting, summarization, keyword mnemonic and imagery less useful. The same article recommends recall over recognition, testing until each item is recalled correctly, then revisiting it on another day, and low-stakes class quizzes. Bjork & Bjork (2011): retrieval acts as a 'memory modifier'; tests have metacognitive benefits; rereading creates familiarity that can be mistaken for understanding.

findings.area: 3b. Spacing (distributed practice)
findings.recommendation: Run a per-learner review queue that brings each learned item or skill back at expanding gaps. Mix recently learned and older material in every session, and make unit quizzes cumulative. Scale the gaps to the time left before the exam (see 6b). Never schedule 'learn it all, review once at the end'.
findings.rationale: Cepeda, Vul, Rohrer, Wixted & Pashler (2008, Psychological Science 19(11):1095–1102), more than 1,350 participants: final performance first rises, then slowly falls, as the gap between study sessions grows. The optimal gap is longer for longer test delays but smaller as a proportion of them: about 20–40% of a 1-week delay and about 5–10% of a 1-year delay. Dunlosky's American Educator article: plan the sessions before an exam, and mix new with older material in each one. Bjork & Bjork (2011): cramming supports short-term performance but little long-term retention; spacing supports both.

findings.area: 3c. Interleaving
findings.recommendation: First teach each problem type with blocked worked examples. Then give mixed practice sets in which consecutive problems need different strategies, so the learner must first identify the problem type (math, physics, chemistry calculations, and categorization tasks such as map or graph reading). Tell learners up front that mixed sets feel harder and lower practice scores, but improve delayed performance. Do not force interleaving on pure memorization items.
findings.rationale: Rohrer, Dedrick, Hartwig & Cheung (2020, J. Educ. Psych. 112(1):40–52), preregistered cluster RCT in 54 7th-grade classes: on an unannounced test one month later, the interleaved group scored 61% vs 38% (d = 0.83). Teachers implemented it without training. Rohrer, Dedrick & Stershic (2015, J. Educ. Psych. 107:900–908) is listed by IES as the project's main result; its effect sizes (d = 0.42 immediate, 0.79 delayed) were seen only in a search snippet of the abstract. Bjork & Bjork (2011) report Rohrer & Taylor (2007): 63% vs 20% correct on new problems a week later. In Kornell & Bjork (2008), most learners believed blocking had helped them more, though interleaving actually did. Dunlosky's article notes interleaving showed no benefit for French vocabulary or comma rules.

findings.area: 3d. Worked examples, faded examples, and self-explanation
findings.recommendation:
For every procedure (e.g., solving a kinematics problem, balancing an equation, reading a statistical chart):
(1) A fully worked example in which the Professor states the principle behind each step.
(2) Faded examples that remove the last step first, then more steps, until the learner solves alone.
(3) At each worked step, an open-ended self-explanation prompt such as 'Which rule justifies this step?' (open text preferred over multiple choice).
(4) An independent problem.
Give more guidance to novices and fade it as accuracy rises.
findings.rationale: Atkinson, Renkl & Merrill (2003, J. Educ. Psych. 95(4):774–783): fading worked-out steps had already been shown to help near transfer. Combining fading with prompts to identify the principle behind each step gave medium-to-large effects on both near and far transfer, with no extra time on task. Bisra et al. (2018, Educational Psychology Review), as reported by BPS Research Digest: 64 studies, about 6,000 participants, g = 0.55. Self-explanation beat instructor-provided explanations; open-ended prompts beat multiple-choice formats; prompts that only ask learners to judge their own knowledge were weaker; the authors advise more guidance for novices. The expertise-reversal effect (Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler & Sweller 2003, Educ. Psychologist 38(1):23–31) is relevant to fading, but only its bibliographic record was verified here.

findings.area: 3e. Dual coding, multimedia principles, and cognitive load (Mayer; Sweller)
findings.recommendation: For each concept, pair the words with one purposeful diagram, and put labels directly on the diagram rather than in a distant legend. Break animations and simulations into learner-paced steps with a 'Continue' button. Before a causal explanation, briefly teach the names and roles of its parts (pretraining). Keep the core flow lean: move fun facts, history and jokes into collapsible asides, and avoid background music or decorative media. Signal structure with headings, an outline, and highlighted key terms. If audio narration is added to an animation, do not also show the same text on screen at the same time, and keep narration synchronized with the visuals. Humor in the dialogue is fine, but tangents count as extraneous material.
findings.rationale:
Mayer & Moreno (2003, Educational Psychologist 38(1):43–52) model learners as having separate verbal and pictorial channels, each with limited capacity, and learning as active processing. Their Table 3 gives median transfer effect sizes, with the number of experiments in brackets:
- modality: 1.17 [6]
- segmenting: 1.36 [1]
- pretraining in component names and behaviors: 1.00 [3]
- coherence (removing interesting but extraneous material): 0.90 [5]
- signaling: 0.74 [1]
- spatial contiguity: 0.48 [1]
- redundancy: 0.69 [3]
- temporal contiguity: 1.30 [8]
When no animation is present, concurrent narration plus on-screen text helped (Moreno & Mayer 2002). The authors flag segmenting, signaling and aligning as single-study results that need more research. They map their terms to cognitive load theory: incidental processing ≈ extraneous load, representational holding ≈ intrinsic load.
findings.license_or_terms: Article PDF carries publisher terms (research/teaching use). Cite, don't redistribute.

findings.area: 3f. Pre-questions (pretesting) and desirable difficulties
findings.recommendation: Open each lesson with 1–2 low-stakes pre-questions on that lesson's crux. Say plainly that wrong answers are expected and are not scored, and answer the questions explicitly inside the lesson. The same items can double as a quick prerequisite diagnostic. Only use difficulties the learner can actually overcome: if the diagnostic shows a missing prerequisite, send the learner to the bridging node first.
findings.rationale: Bjork & Bjork (2011) summarize Kornell, Hays & Bjork (2009): tests can make later study more effective even when learners are certain to answer wrong. They list desirable difficulties as varying conditions, interleaving, spacing, and using tests as study events. They stress that a difficulty is 'desirable' only if the learner has the background knowledge to respond successfully; otherwise it becomes undesirable. Pan & Carpenter (2023, Educational Psychology Review 35:97) conclude that prequestions and pretests can often enhance learning, with the size varying by procedure. This was seen only in search-result abstract text; the full text was not verified.

findings.area: 3g. Refutation texts for misconceptions
findings.rationale: Schroeder & Kucera (2022, Educational Psychology Review 34(2):957–987) meta-analysis: 44 comparisons, n = 3,869, g = 0.41 vs other conditions. The effect was robust across domain, age, prior knowledge, length and test timing. They define refutation text as stating a misconception, refuting it, and explaining the correct conception. Muller et al. (2008): Refutation 0.79 and Dialogue 0.83 vs Exposition, with the largest benefit for low-prior-knowledge students. Caution from Chi et al. (2017): the content of tutee errors did not by itself predict observers' learning. What tracked learning was the extra constructive engagement after errors, so always pair the refutation with a reader task.

findings.area: 3h. Mastery learning and progress states
findings.recommendation:
Give each knowledge node visible levels, for example 未開始/Not started → 嘗試/Attempted → 熟悉/Familiar → 精熟/Proficient → 掌握/Mastered.
- Advance a node only on a criterion score on mixed items.
- After a miss, route the learner to a targeted corrective (often a prerequisite node), then a fresh parallel check.
- Mastered nodes keep reappearing in spaced mixed reviews, so nothing is permanently 'done'.
- Report progress as 'nodes at Proficient or above', not time spent.
findings.rationale: Khan Academy (efficacy blog, 2023, updated 2025) describes four levels: attempted, familiar, proficient, mastered. Its 'skills to proficient' metric was associated with scores on the external MAP Growth math test regardless of time or number of skills attempted. The post recommends reaching at least proficient on fewer skills and retrying exercises that don't reach it. Chi et al. (2017) cite one-to-one tutoring as the gold standard (Bloom 1984) with an average d ≈ 0.79 (VanLehn 2011). Kulik, Kulik & Bangert-Drowns (1990, RER 60(2):265–299) meta-analyzed mastery learning programs; the bibliographic record was verified, but the pooled effect size was not.
findings.license_or_terms: Concept only; do not copy Khan Academy UI or assets.

findings.area: 4. Preventing 'jumping too fast': prerequisite graph, define-before-use, pacing
findings.rationale: 均一 (Junyi) describes its knowledge map as the relationships between knowledge points, e.g., what must come before learning circle area. It was built from learners' data and then adjusted by its education team; the 2019 post names 國小數學 (elementary math). A 2018 數位時代 report describes the planned design: a prerequisite example (learning 速率/speed needs 除法/division and 單位/units first) and prompts that point a stuck student to the missing foundation. Mayer & Moreno (2003): pretraining on component names and behaviors, d = 1.00 across 3 experiments. Bjork & Bjork (2011): without background knowledge, difficulties become undesirable. OSTEP orders concurrency after virtualization for exactly this reason. The build-check rule is a design inference built on these sources, not a tested intervention.
findings.license_or_terms: Junyi / Khan Academy: concept only, no reuse of their content.

findings.area: 5a. Bilingual site UX: language switch, URL structure, remembering the preference
findings.recommendation:
(1) Give each language its own URL using mirrored subdirectories (e.g., /zh-tw/math/... and /en/math/... with identical slugs). Do not swap languages only through a cookie on a single URL.
(2) Put a clearly visible switcher on every page that links to the same lesson in the other language. Label the options in their own language and script ('中文（台灣）' / 'English') so someone who can't read the current page can find it.
(3) Remember the explicit choice (cookie/localStorage, or the profile if logged in) and honor it on later visits.
(4) Use the browser's Accept-Language only as a first-visit default. Never force-redirect, and never choose the language by IP address.
(5) Add hreflang alternates between the paired pages.
(6) Keep main content and navigation in the same language on each page.
(7) Set the html lang attribute to a short, correct tag (zh-Hant or zh-TW / zh-Hant-TW; en). Mark inline zh terms on English pages with their own lang attribute.
findings.rationale: Google Search Central: use a different URL for each language rather than cookies or browser settings; subdirectories and subdomains are the listed options. Don't auto-redirect users based on a guess of their language. Add visible links to other language versions. Use hreflang or sitemaps. Don't adapt content by IP analysis. Avoid pages whose boilerplate is translated but whose main content is not. W3C 'When to use language negotiation': negotiation needs manual overrides; switch links belong on all pages except non-equivalent sets; they must be understandable to someone who can't read the current language; the explicit choice should be sticky (session cookie, user profile, or language-specific links). W3C 'Choosing a language tag': keep tags as short as possible, and add script or region subtags only when they distinguish something.

findings.area: 5b. Helping English readers who sit a Chinese-language exam
findings.recommendation:
(1) In English mode, show the official zh-TW term next to the English term at its first use in every lesson, e.g., 'acceleration（加速度）', placed adjacent rather than in a footnote. Offer a hover or tap card with the term, pinyin/zhuyin if wanted, and a definition.
(2) Keep a per-lesson bilingual glossary plus a site-wide glossary generated from the knowledge map's 'terms introduced' field.
(3) Standardize every zh–en term pair against 國家教育研究院 樂詞網 (its high-school subject term lists) and record the source for each pair.
(4) Every practice item in English mode gets a '顯示中文 / show in Chinese' toggle. From mid-course on, assign some reviews in Chinese, and make the final mock exams Chinese-only, as the real exam is (except the English paper).
(5) Do not show full parallel EN/ZH paragraphs side by side by default. Keep that as an opt-in 'parallel' view, to avoid redundant reading load. This is a design inference from Mayer's redundancy and coherence findings, not tested for bilingual text.
findings.rationale: 樂詞網 is run by NAER (國家教育研究院). It includes term lists for 高中以下 chemistry, IT, mathematics, geography, physics, earth science and life science, plus bilingual vocabulary and textbook terms, so it can serve as the authority for standard zh-TW terms. Mayer & Moreno (2003) support placing words next to what they label (spatial contiguity, d = 0.48, one study). Language-dependent memory: Marian & Fausey (2006, Applied Cognitive Psychology 20(8):1025–1047). The bibliographic record was verified. The reported finding, from search summaries only, is that highly proficient bilinguals recalled academic content better when the test language matched the learning language. This supports practicing retrieval in Chinese before the exam, but it is flagged as not verified against the abstract or full text.
findings.license_or_terms: Use 樂詞網 as a reference authority for term pairs; check its terms of use before bulk-downloading or redistributing its lists.

findings.area: 6a. Exam-prep layer: using past 學測 papers ethically (link vs embed)
findings.recommendation:
(1) Deep-link each official past paper, answer key and 非選擇題評分原則 (constructed-response scoring guide) on ceec.edu.tw by year, subject and question number. Do not re-host the PDFs or DOCX files.
(2) Build in-site practice from original items written to the same 學習內容 and 學測 item style, clearly labeled as original, not official.
(3) When a worked solution discusses an official item, cite it (e.g., '115學測 數學A 第x題'), link to it, and quote only the minimum needed. Never reproduce third-party literary or reading passages embedded in 國文/英文/社會 items.
(4) Keep the site non-commercial unless written permission is obtained. Ask 大考中心 for written authorization before embedding any full paper.
(5) Use CEEC's published 評分原則 for self-grading rubrics, linked rather than copied.
findings.rationale:
CEEC's 一般試題 page posts, per year and subject, the 試題 (PDF/DOCX), 答題卷 (answer sheet), 選擇題答案 (multiple-choice key) and 非選擇題評分原則. The 115 set was posted 115-02-23. The page footer reads 大學入學考試中心 版權所有 © 2026; no specific reuse terms for the files were found. Legal status is unsettled:
- 章忠信 (2011) argues that 學測 papers are 'exam questions held under law' under Copyright Act §9(1)(5), so not copyrightable, while CEEC can still grant authorization.
- 智慧財產局 (TIPO) e-mail interpretation 1090203b (2020) would not say whether 學測 qualifies and refers the question to 教育部 / the exam authority.
- In 2019 CEEC relied on §54 (reproduction for exams held by schools and educational institutions) to excerpt authors' works, did not notify the authors, and then said it would stop using those authors.
Therefore a third-party site that re-hosts those passages is not clearly covered (inference). Linking avoids the issue and keeps learners on the current official version.
findings.license_or_terms: CEEC site: '版權所有 © 2026'. Whether 學測 試題 fall under §9(1)(5) is disputed: 章忠信 says yes; TIPO defers to MOE. Embedded third-party passages were reproduced by CEEC under §54. Link, don't re-host; get written permission for embedding.

findings.area: 6b. Spaced review up to exam day (116學年度學測)
findings.recommendation:
Add a countdown planner anchored to the 116學測 dates: 2027-01-22 數學A + 自然; 2027-01-23 英文 + 國綜 + 國寫; 2027-01-24 數學B + 社會. From 2026-11-15 that is 68 days to the first exam day.
- Work backward from the exam. Each learned node gets reviews at expanding gaps that shrink as a share of the time remaining. For a horizon of about 10 weeks, gaps of roughly 1–2 weeks between reviews of the same node is an interpolation between Cepeda's 1-week (20–40%) and 1-year (5–10%) points, not a tested value.
- Every session mixes new and old material.
- Final 2–3 weeks: interleaved, timed mock sets grouped like the real exam days, using linked CEEC past papers and CEEC 評分原則 for self-scoring; no new content in the last days.
- Warn against cramming.
- Show the official milestones: 應考資訊/試場查詢 from 2027-01-05; score query from 2027-02-25.
findings.rationale: Dates come from the 自由時報 report of 2026-10-23 on the CEEC announcement (exam 2027-01-22 to 24, subjects per day, registration 2026-10-27 to 11-10). The CEEC homepage lists 116學年度 notices, including registration closing 115-11-10 and the 試務專区, and CEEC's 試務專區 gives venue query 2027-01-05 to 01-24 and score query from 2027-02-25. Cepeda et al. (2008) give the gap ratios. Dunlosky (AFT) says to plan sessions before the exam and mix old with new. Bjork & Bjork (2011): cramming gives short-term performance with little retention. The official 116 簡章 PDF was fetched but could not be parsed; its dates were seen only in a search snippet, consistent with the above.

open_questions: OSTEP's authors do not name a specific inspiration for the dialogue format. The preface only calls it 'one of the oldest didactic methods'; Feynman's Six Easy Pieces inspired the title only. No other stated source was found.
OSTEP version is inconsistent: the website lists v1.10 (Nov 2023), but the preface PDF footer says v1.20 with © 2008–26. This is cosmetic but should be cited carefully.

CEEC reuse terms: only the site footer '版權所有 © 2026' was seen. Search snippets show CEEC 考試說明 PDFs carrying a copyright plus non-commercial notice, but those files were not opened. Need direct confirmation from 大考中心 (and possibly 教育部) on whether linking, quoting single items, or embedding full papers is allowed, and whether 學測 試題 count as §9(1)(5) exam questions. TIPO declined to decide.
The 116學年度 簡章 PDF (ceec.edu.tw) could not be parsed. Exam dates rest on the 自由時報 report of the CEEC announcement plus CEEC portal pages; the per-day time slots were not verified.
Pan & Carpenter (2023) prequestioning review: only search-result abstract text was seen; the full-text recommendations were not verified.
Kulik, Kulik & Bangert-Drowns (1990): pooled mastery-learning effect size not verified (only the bibliographic record was opened).

Marian & Fausey (2006) language-dependent memory: findings seen only in search summaries; the abstract and full text were not opened. The recommendation to rehearse in Chinese before the exam rests partly on it.
Rohrer, Dedrick & Stershic (2015) effect sizes (d = 0.42 / 0.79) come from search snippets of the abstract. The 2020 RCT figures were verified via Semantic Scholar.
Kalyuga et al. (2003) expertise reversal effect: only bibliographic metadata was verified.
Khan Academy's current level-up and demotion rules were not verified (the support page returned 403); only the efficacy blog's description of the four levels was confirmed.

W3C guidance on using flags in language switchers was not found. Only secondary blogs (not opened) advise against flags, so the 'name languages in their own script' advice rests on W3C's general requirement that the switcher be understandable to someone who can't read the current language.
Whether 均一's knowledge map now covers secondary (國中/高中) subjects is unknown. The 2019 source names 國小數學 only.

No research was gathered specifically on bilingual glossaries for learners who study in L1 but sit a content exam in L2 (the Kieffer et al. 2009 accommodations meta-analysis findings could not be opened). The web-search budget ran out before this could be pursued; a follow-up is needed.
Which misconceptions to refute in each 學測 topic still needs sourcing, e.g., CEEC 試題分析 / 選擇題答題分析 per subject, or published misconception research, so that no misconception is invented.
Mapping each lesson node to exact 十二年國教 課綱 學習內容 codes (NAER documents) was outside this thread and must come from the curriculum-research thread.

verification.topic: Fact-check of 'Pedagogy & dialogue format' research report (OSTEP dialogue format, learning-science evidence, prerequisite mapping, bilingual UX, 學測 exam-prep layer)

confirmed.claim: OSTEP preface: the dialogue is 'one of the oldest didactic methods'. It is used to introduce the major thematic concepts ('in a peachy way') and to review material now and then, and is 'a chance to write in a more humorous style'. The preface also describes: the explicit 'crux of the problem'; timelines of behavior over time; asides and tips, all indexed at the back; and homework simulators where 'by giving them a different random seed, you can generate a virtually infinite set of problems', which the simulators can also solve.

OSTEP 'To Educators': concurrency is 'pushed off' until students understand CPU and memory virtualization. The reason given is that students have a hard time understanding how the concurrency problem arises without knowing what an address space and a process are, or why context switches can happen at arbitrary points.

OSTEP preface footnote 4: 'free' does not mean open source, and the book is copyrighted 'with the usual protections'. The authors want 'a single voice throughout', and the book should 'feel like a dialogue with the person explaining'. The preface also asks readers to link to the online chapters rather than make local copies. The title is an homage to Feynman's lecture notes (reference F96 is Six Easy Pieces). Footer: '© 2008-26, ARPACI-DUSSEAU' and '[VERSION 1.20]'.

OSTEP website: v1.10, November 2023. The book 'is and will always be free in PDF form'. Instructors are asked to 'please just link to them directly'. Summary dialogues are chapters 11, 24, 34, 46 and 51. Opening dialogues are chapters 1, 3, 12, 25, 35 and 52, plus unnumbered dialogues for VMM, monitors and labs.

The three dialogues the report opened each have about 2 pages of content: the Dialogue on the Book, the Dialogue on Virtualization, and the Summary Dialogue on CPU Virtualization. The virtualization PDF is 4 pages, but that count includes a Part title page and a blank page. The virtualization dialogue uses the physical-vs-virtual peach analogy and then moves to the CPU. In the CPU summary, the Student lists traps, timer interrupts and context-switch state saving, and the Professor asks about the 'philosophy of the OS'. In Dialogue 1 the Professor says it is useful to 'pull yourself outside of a narrative and think a bit'.

Chi, Roy & Hausmann (2008), Cognitive Science 32(2):301–341. Students who collaboratively observed tutoring videos learned physics problem-solving about as well as the tutees. Tutoring was most effective when tutees constructed knowledge themselves or jointly with the tutor, and less effective when the tutor only conveyed information.

Chi, Kang & Yaghmourian (2017), J. Learning Sciences 26(1):10–50. Average video lengths were 25 min (dialogue) vs 21 min (monologue), p = .28. On 11 deeper transfer questions, the dialogue-observers' gain was d = 1.08 (tutees d = 1.07), and an ANCOVA found no difference from the tutees. Dialogue-observers solved 16.70 workbook problems vs copied 5.30, out of 22. Tutor and tutee moves did not directly correlate with observers' learning. Observers did the same workbook/worksheets. The paper cites tutoring at d ≈ 0.79 (VanLehn 2011) as the gold standard (Bloom 1984), and uses the ICAP framework.

Muller, Sharma, Eklund & Reimann (2007), Instructional Science 35(6):519–533, on quantum tunneling: the dialogue video beat the expository video, d = 0.71. Muller, Bewes, Sharma & Reimann, JCAL 24:144–155 (online 2007, print 2008): n = 364, Newton's First and Second Laws. Effect sizes vs Exposition: Refutation 0.79, Dialogue 0.83. 'Students with low prior knowledge benefited most.' The bibliographic details were confirmed via Crossref/Semantic Scholar; the effect sizes come from a blog post that reproduces the abstracts.

Ginns, Martin & Marsh (2013), Educational Psychology Review 25(4):445–472. Results: retention d = 0.30, transfer d = 0.54, friendliness d = 0.46. There were 'small, non-significant effects being found in studies longer than 35 min'. Conversational style in this meta-analysis includes second-person address and politer forms of address.
Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Psychological Science 17(3):249–255. Restudying was better at 5 minutes. Prior testing gave much better retention at 2 days and 1 week. Restudying increased confidence.

Dunlosky, American Educator, Fall 2013. Practice testing and distributed practice are rated most effective. Interleaving, elaborative interrogation and self-explanation are 'promising'. Rereading, highlighting, summarization, keyword mnemonic and imagery are less useful. The article recommends recall over recognition, testing until each item is recalled correctly at least once and then relearning it on another day, and a low-stakes quiz at the start of each class. It also says to plan study sessions before the exam and mix new with old material. Interleaving showed no benefit for French vocabulary or for high-school comma rules. The PSPI article (Dunlosky et al. 2013, 14(1)) exists as cited.

Bjork & Bjork (2011), 'Making Things Hard on Yourself, But in a Good Way'. Retrieval is a 'memory modifier' (Bjork 1975). Tests have metacognitive benefits, and tests potentiate later study even when learners are sure to be wrong (Kornell, Hays & Bjork 2009). Desirable difficulties named: varying conditions, interleaving, spacing, and tests as study events. Difficulties 'become undesirable' if the learner lacks the background knowledge. Rohrer & Taylor (2007): 63% vs 20% a week later. In Kornell & Bjork (2008), the majority thought blocking was more effective. Cramming gives short-term performance, and rereading creates familiarity that can be confused with understanding.

Cepeda, Vul, Rohrer, Wixted & Pashler (2008), Psychological Science 19(11):1095–1102. More than 1,350 participants. Performance rises and then falls as the study gap grows. The optimal gap is about 20–40% of a 1-week test delay and about 5–10% of a 1-year delay.

Rohrer, Dedrick, Hartwig & Cheung, J. Educ. Psych. 112(1):40–52 (2020; online-first 2019). Preregistered cluster RCT in 54 7th-grade classes over 4 months. On an unannounced test one month later, interleaved scored 61% vs blocked 38%, d = 0.83. Teachers implemented it without training. Nuance: both groups also did an interleaved review assignment before the test.

Rohrer, Dedrick & Stershic (2015), J. Educ. Psych. 107:900–908. The abstract, now verified via Semantic Scholar, reports 126 seventh-graders and an unannounced test 1 or 30 days after the review. Interleaved practice was better on both tests: Cohen's d = 0.42 (1-day test) and 0.79 (30-day test).

Atkinson, Renkl & Merrill (2003), J. Educ. Psych. 95(4):774–783. Fading alone reliably helped near transfer, but its far-transfer effects were inconsistent. Fading combined with principle-identification prompts gave medium-to-large effects on near and far transfer without extra time on task.

Bisra et al. (2018), Educational Psychology Review, as reported by BPS Research Digest: 64 studies, nearly 6,000 participants, g = 0.55. Self-explanation beat instructor explanation. Multiple-choice prompt formats were least effective, and metacognitive 'judge your knowledge' prompts were weaker. The ideal level of guidance depends on proficiency.

Mayer & Moreno (2003), 'Nine Ways to Reduce Cognitive Load in Multimedia Learning', Educational Psychologist 38(1):43–52. Table 3 median effect sizes, with number of experiments: modality 1.17 (6); segmenting 1.36 (1); pretraining 1.00 (3); coherence/weeding 0.90 (5); signaling 0.74 (1); spatial contiguity 0.48 (1); redundancy 0.69 (3); temporal contiguity 1.30 (8). With no animation, concurrent narration plus on-screen text helped (Moreno & Mayer 2002, Exps 1 and 3). The authors say segmenting, signaling and aligning rest on single preliminary studies and need more research. Incidental processing ≈ extraneous load, and representational holding ≈ intrinsic load. The 'Continue' button segmenting example is in the text.

Pan & Carpenter (2023), Educational Psychology Review 35(4), article 97, DOI 10.1007/s10648-023-09814-5. The abstract, now verified via Crossref, says prequestions and pretests 'can often enhance learning', with the size varying by procedure and outcome measure. This verifies the abstract only, not the full text.

Schroeder & Kucera (2022), Educational Psychology Review 34(2):957–987. 44 comparisons from 33 studies, n = 3,869, g = 0.41 (95% CI 0.30–0.51). Refutation text is defined as stating a misconception, refuting it, and explaining the correct conception. The effect was robust across domain, age, prior knowledge, text length and test timing. Publication type was the one significant moderator; the report omits this.

Khan Academy efficacy post 'Why Khan Academy will be using skills to proficient...', by Bogdan Yamkovenko, dated 2023-09-25 and updated 2025-03-21. Four levels: attempted, familiar, proficient, mastered. Skills-to-proficient correlated with MAP Growth math scores regardless of time spent or number of skills attempted. The post recommends reaching at least proficient on fewer skills and retrying exercises that don't reach it. This is an in-house, correlational analysis.

均一 2019-05-30 post: the 知識地圖 shows the relationships between knowledge points, with the example of 圓面積的計算. It was built from learners' data and then adjusted by the 均一 education team, for 國小數學. 數位時代, 2018-08-13: the 速率 example needs 除法 and 單位 first. Prompts would tell stuck students which foundations to fill in. This was described as a planned launch ('預計最快8月底上線').

Google Search Central recommends: different URLs per language rather than cookies or browser settings; subdirectories, subdomains or ccTLDs (URL parameters not recommended); avoid automatically redirecting based on a guess of the user's language; add hyperlinks to other language versions; use hreflang or sitemaps; 'Don't use IP analysis to adapt your content'; and avoid translating only the boilerplate.

W3C 'When to use language negotiation': manual language controls are needed; they belong on all pages except sets that are not sufficiently equivalent; they must be usable by someone unfamiliar with the current page's language. Stickiness can come from a session cookie, a user profile, or language-specific links. The page does not mention flags. W3C 'Choosing a language tag': 'keep your language tag as short as possible'; add script or region subtags only when they add distinguishing information.

樂詞網 is run by 國家教育研究院. Its 教科書名詞 category lists 高中以下 term sets for 化學, 資訊, 數學, 地理學, 物理學, 地球科學 and 生命科學. 雙語詞彙 and 學術名詞 categories also exist. Footer: 'Copyright © 2021 國家教育研究院 版權所有'. No explicit reuse license was found on the homepage.

CEEC 一般試題 page: each subject of 115學年度學科能力測驗 was posted 115-02-23 with 試題 (PDF and DOCX), 答題卷, 選擇題答案 and 非選擇題評分原則. 國寫 has no 選擇題答案. The footer reads '大學入學考試中心 版權所有 © 2026 All Rights Reserved.' No file-specific reuse terms are on the page.
著作權法 §9(1)(5) excludes from copyright '依法令舉行之各類考試試題及其備用試題'. §54 lets exams held by 中央或地方機關、依法設立之各級學校或教育機構 reproduce published works '供為試題之用'.

章忠信, '大考中心徵題，著作權歸誰？' (100.07.04 = 2011). Because 大考中心 holds exams under 大學法 §24, its items fall under §9(1)(5) and are not copyrightable. 大考中心 can still 'authorize' use, but this rests on its credibility, not on copyright.
TIPO 電子郵件1090203b (109-02-03): TIPO does not decide whether 國中基測 or 大學學測 are 依法令舉行之考試試題, and refers the question to 教育部 or the exam's competent authority.
2019 CNA report on Yahoo, '大考中心：著作不再入學測題'. 劉孟奇 cited 著作權法 §54. Authors (馬世芳, 張曉風) were not notified in advance, for secrecy reasons. CEEC said it would re-examine the question bank.

116學測 dates. 自由時報 (2026-10-23): exam 2027-01-22 to 24. 1/22 數學A + 自然; 1/23 英文 + 國綜 + 國寫; 1/24 數學B + 社會. Registration 10/27–11/10. The CEEC primary '116學年度考試重要試務日期' PDF shows 116.01.22~116.01.24 in the column whose registration dates (115.10.27~115.11.10) and 116.02.25 score date match 學測. Its Chinese labels are not machine-extractable, so the column is identified by matching dates. From 2026-11-15 to 2027-01-22 is 68 days.

CEEC 試務專區 (116 學測) dates. Registration 115.10.27–115.11.10. 報名結果檢核 115.11.13–11.19. 試場地點查詢 116.01.05–01.24. 應考資訊查詢 from 116.01.05. 成績查詢 from 116.02.25. 複查 application 116.02.26–03.04. The CEEC homepage lists the 115-11-06 press release on registration closing 115-11-10, and the 試務專區 link.

corrections.original: OSTEP table of contents: opening 'Dialogue' chapters 1, 3, 12, 25, 35, 52, 'plus VMM, monitors, distribution and labs' (grouping distribution with the unnumbered dialogues).
corrections.correction: The distribution dialogue is a numbered chapter, ch. 47 (dialogue-distribution.pdf). Only the VMM, monitors and labs dialogues are unnumbered in the TOC. Opening dialogues are therefore chs. 1, 3, 12, 25, 35, 47 and 52.

corrections.original: OSTEP version: 'the preface footer says v1.20 with © 2008–26, while the website lists v1.10 (Nov 2023)'.
corrections.correction: This is accurate but incomplete, so the book should be cited as 'v1.10, with some chapters updated'. The individual dialogue chapter PDFs still carry '[VERSION 1.10]' footers. The preface's own citation block lists 'October, 2023 (Version 1.10)', not November, alongside v1.00 (Aug 2018) and v1.01 (Jul 2019).

corrections.original: 'Rohrer, Dedrick & Stershic (2015) ... is listed by IES as the project's main result; its effect sizes (d = 0.42 immediate, 0.79 delayed) were seen only in a search snippet.'
corrections.correction: The IES award page (R305A110517) lists the 2015 paper among five publications under 'Products and publications'. It does not call it the main result and reports no findings. The effect sizes are now verified from the abstract via Semantic Scholar: 126 seventh-graders, unannounced test 1 or 30 days later, d = 0.42 and 0.79. The 0.42 test came 1 day later, so it is not an 'immediate' test.

corrections.original: Caveat in 2a: 'these studies used college students, mostly lab settings'.
corrections.correction: The settings were mixed. Muller et al. (2007) is titled 'in an authentic physics setting': second-year students watched the video during a lecture. Muller et al. (2008) used online multimedia with 364 first-year physics students. The Chi studies were lab studies. The college-student caveat stands, and the transfer to high-school (學測) learners is untested.

corrections.original: 'In 2019 CEEC ... then said it would stop using those authors.'
corrections.correction: Per the CNA report, CEEC said it would re-examine the question bank and recommend that item writers not use these authors' works again. This is an advisory recommendation, not a formal ban.

corrections.original: 5b: '樂詞網 ... can serve as the authority for standard zh-TW terms' and 'Standardize every zh–en term pair against 樂詞網 (its high-school subject term lists)'.
corrections.correction: The 高中以下 教科書名詞 lists cover only 化學, 資訊, 數學, 地理學, 物理學, 地球科學 and 生命科學. No 高中以下 list for 歷史, 公民與社會 or 國文 was found. That covers two of the three Social Studies subjects, plus the Chinese beta. For those subjects the plan needs another documented source (e.g., 樂詞網 學術名詞 sets, if they exist for those fields, which was not verified) or must flag the term pairs as editorial.

corrections.original: 5a(7): 'Set the html lang attribute to a short, correct tag (zh-Hant or zh-TW / zh-Hant-TW; en)', attributed to W3C 'Choosing a language tag'.
corrections.correction: The W3C page gives only the general rules (keep tags short; add script/region subtags only when they add distinguishing information). It does not mention zh-Hant, zh-TW or zh-Hant-TW. The Chinese tag choice is an inference from those rules, not explicit W3C guidance.

corrections.original: 3g rationale lists robust moderators for Schroeder & Kucera (2022) without exceptions.
corrections.correction: Publication type was a significant moderator (Q_b(2) = 9.01, p = 0.01). The other listed moderators were non-significant. Some, such as reading level, were reported in few studies.

corrections.original: Open question: 'Pan & Carpenter (2023) ... only search-result abstract text was seen'.
corrections.correction: The Crossref record confirms Educational Psychology Review 35(4), article 97, DOI 10.1007/s10648-023-09814-5. Its abstract says prequestioning and pretesting 'can often enhance learning', with the size varying by procedure and outcome measure. The full-text recommendations remain unverified.

unverifiable.claim: Marian & Fausey (2006): highly proficient bilinguals recalled academic content better when test language matched learning language.
unverifiable.reason: Crossref confirms Applied Cognitive Psychology 20(8):1025–1047. Crossref and Semantic Scholar both withhold the abstract, and the WebSearch budget for this run was exhausted, so the finding was not checked against the paper.

unverifiable.claim: Kulik, Kulik & Bangert-Drowns (1990) pooled mastery-learning effect size.
unverifiable.reason: Semantic Scholar has the title, authors and year only; the publisher withholds the abstract. The full text was not accessible.

unverifiable.claim: Specific effect sizes for Atkinson, Renkl & Merrill (2003).
unverifiable.reason: The abstract says only 'medium to large'. No numeric values were seen.

unverifiable.claim: Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler & Sweller (2003) expertise-reversal findings as applied to fading.
unverifiable.reason: Only Crossref metadata was verified (Educational Psychologist 38(1):23–31). The content was not checked. The second cited DOI, S15326985EP3801_3, is Renkl & Atkinson (2003), 38(1):15–22, which the report lists but does not discuss.

unverifiable.claim: Per-day subject allocation of 116學測 (1/22 數A+自然; 1/23 英文+國綜+國寫; 1/24 數B+社會) and time slots.
unverifiable.reason: Confirmed only in 自由時報. The CEEC 重要試務日期 PDF shows the 116.01.22–01.24 date range, but its labels are not text-extractable. The CEEC 試務專區 page has no per-day timetable. The 簡章 was not parsed.

unverifiable.claim: Reuse terms for CEEC past-paper PDF/DOCX files (link vs embed).
unverifiable.reason: Only the site footer '版權所有 © 2026' was found. The legal status depends on whether 學測 counts as 依法令舉行之考試: 章忠信 says yes, and TIPO defers to 教育部. Written confirmation from CEEC is still needed.

unverifiable.claim: Muller et al. (2008) effect sizes (Refutation 0.79, Dialogue 0.83) and Muller et al. (2007) d = 0.71.
unverifiable.reason: These come from a physics-education blog that reproduces the abstracts. The publisher records on Crossref and Semantic Scholar withhold the abstracts, so the values were not checked against the primary source.

unverifiable.claim: Whether 均一's knowledge map now covers 國中/高中 subjects; Khan Academy's current level-up and demotion rules.
unverifiable.reason: The sources found describe 國小數學 (2019) and a 2018 plan. No current documentation was checked, and the web search budget was exhausted.

unverifiable.claim: 樂詞網 terms of use for bulk download or redistribution.
unverifiable.reason: The homepage shows only a copyright notice. The linked 政府網站資料開放宣告 page was not opened.

verification.notes:
Overall, the report is accurate. I found no invented citations, and the numbers I checked match their primary sources: OSTEP, Chi 2017, Ginns, Cepeda, Rohrer, Mayer & Moreno Table 3, Schroeder & Kucera, Khan, 均一, Google, W3C, CEEC, the 著作權法, and TIPO. The errors are minor: one mislabeled OSTEP chapter, an overstated IES attribution, an imprecise setting caveat, a soft paraphrase of the 2019 CEEC statement, and an unflagged inference about W3C language tags.

The substantive gap is the 樂詞網 claim: it has no 高中以下 term lists for 歷史, 公民 or 國文, which matters for the Social Studies and Chinese-beta parts of the plan.

The 116學測 date range is now corroborated by a CEEC primary PDF, read by matching dates in its columns.

Limits of this check:
- The WebSearch budget for this run was exhausted after the first query, so I could not run independent Traditional-Chinese searches. All verification was done by fetching cited or official URLs directly, plus Crossref and Semantic Scholar DOI lookups.
- PDFs were read with local pdftotext/PyMuPDF on cached copies; no project files were modified.
- The report does not use 課綱 學習內容 codes, so there was nothing in that area to check. Its own recommendations (the build-time define-before-use check, the gap interpolation, and the bilingual parallel-view advice) are correctly flagged as design inferences.

research.topic: Web platform for a bilingual (en + zh-TW) GSAT zero-to-hero course site: Astro i18n, math and chemistry rendering, science and map visuals, CJK search, Traditional Chinese typography, static hosting. Researched 2026-11-15. The WebSearch budget ran out partway through, so everything after that was checked by opening primary pages directly with WebFetch.

findings.area: 1. Framework baseline and Markdown pipeline (affects every plugin choice)
findings.recommendation: Build on Astro 7.x, the same major version as the owner's reference project (it pins astro ^7.4.12, @astrojs/mdx ^8.1.6, @astrojs/react ^7.1.9, react ^19.3.1, pagefind ^1.6.0). Keep the explicit `markdown.processor: unified({ remarkPlugins, rehypePlugins })` from @astrojs/markdown-remark that the reference project already uses for its custom remark-dialogue plugin. Do NOT switch to Astro 7's default Sätteri processor for now: remark-math, rehype-katex and the custom dialogue/glossary remark plugins only run under unified(). Other notes: use Node >= 22.12 (Astro 6+ requirement). Import z from 'astro/zod' (Zod 4). Put collections in src/content.config.ts with a glob() loader. Watch for Astro 7's compressHTML:'jsx' default: whitespace between inline elements is stripped, so mixed zh/en inline markup can lose spaces. Use {' '} or set compressHTML:true.
findings.rationale: Astro 7.0 (2026-06-22) made Sätteri, a Rust processor, the default. Existing remark/rehype plugins need @astrojs/markdown-remark with unified(). Sätteri can only parse math (opt-in). It does not render math, and remark/rehype plugins do not run on it unmodified. The only KaTeX port for Sätteri found is a community repo (satteri-katex, MIT, about 12 stars, 0.1.x), which is too immature to build a course on. Per the docs, unified() renders both .md and .mdx. The latest release found is Astro 7.4 (2026-10-15).
findings.license_or_terms: Astro: MIT (not re-verified this session). @astrojs/markdown-remark is part of Astro.

findings.area: 1a. Astro built-in i18n routing configuration
findings.recommendation: Use plain string locale codes, which work with fully static output: `i18n: { locales: ['zh-tw','en'], defaultLocale: 'zh-tw', routing: { prefixDefaultLocale: true, redirectToDefaultLocale: false } }`. Make src/pages/index.astro a small bilingual language-chooser landing page (also the hreflang x-default target) instead of an automatic redirect. Put the pages under src/pages/zh-tw/ and src/pages/en/; folder names must match the locale strings exactly. Avoid the `{ path, codes }` object form and `domains` for a static site. Use `fallback: { en: 'zh-tw' }` only if you deliberately want untranslated English URLs to exist. If you do, prefer the default fallbackType 'redirect'. 'rewrite' writes the zh-tw content at /en/... URLs, so the layout must set <html lang> from the entry's real language, not from Astro.currentLocale. Add a 'not yet translated' banner, and keep those pages out of hreflang and search.
findings.rationale: Docs: prefixDefaultLocale defaults to false. With true, every locale, including the default, gets a folder, and unprefixed URLs return 404 unless a fallback is set. Astro 6 changed redirectToDefaultLocale to default false, and it can only be enabled with prefixDefaultLocale:true. fallbackType 'rewrite' (since 4.15) builds files like dist/fr/about.html containing the fallback language's content. Astro 6.1 made @astrojs/sitemap include those fallback pages automatically, so rewrite fallbacks would publish duplicate-language URLs. The domains feature needs server output plus a node/vercel adapter. The docs' Limitations wording also seems to say custom { path, codes } paths need output:'server', but that wording is ambiguous. Google advises against automatic language-based redirects and recommends visible language-switch links.
findings.license_or_terms: n/a

findings.area: 1b. Content collections per locale: parallel per-locale MDX vs single-file bilingual
findings.recommendation: Use parallel per-locale MDX files with mirrored ASCII relative paths: src/content/lessons/zh-tw/math/01-numbers.mdx and src/content/lessons/en/math/01-numbers.mdx. Use one `lessons` collection (glob loader, pattern '**/*.mdx'). Write a custom generateId that keeps the path minus its extension, so the id is '<locale>/<subject>/<slug>' and a translation is found by swapping the first segment. Add a frontmatter field such as `translationOf`/`lessonKey` plus a `status: draft|reviewed` field. A build-time check can then list lessons missing a translation and block links to them. Keep language-neutral assets once: widget code, quiz answer keys, diagram data, and glossary IDs. Load UI strings and widget labels from a per-locale dictionary (src/i18n/ui.ts with a t() helper, as in Astro's i18n recipe). Make the recipe's silent fallback for missing keys a build error. Do not put both languages in one page toggled by JS.
findings.rationale: Google recommends a separate URL for each language version and warns against translating only the interface chrome. Pagefind reads one <html lang> per page and builds a separate index per language. Browsers also use lang for CJK font and glyph selection. A single-file bilingual page with a JS toggle would break search, hreflang and glyph selection. The glob loader's default IDs come from github-slugger, and the docs do not say how non-ASCII (Chinese) filenames are slugged. ASCII filenames plus a custom generateId keep IDs predictable. Astro's own i18n recipe uses src/content/<collection>/<lang>/ folders, and it notes that missing UI keys silently fall back to the default language. deferRender (Astro 7.1) can postpone Markdown rendering until a page needs it.
findings.license_or_terms: n/a

findings.area: 1c. hreflang, sitemap and a language switcher that keeps the same page
findings.recommendation: In the base layout, emit <link rel="alternate" hreflang="zh-TW" ...>, <link ... hreflang="en" ...> and hreflang="x-default" (pointing to the root chooser). Emit an alternate only when that locale's version actually exists, and use fully qualified URLs, so you need `site` set. Every version must list itself and all others. Also enable @astrojs/sitemap (v3.7.5 per docs) with `i18n: { defaultLocale: 'zh-tw', locales: { 'zh-tw': 'zh-TW', en: 'en' } }`, which writes xhtml:link alternates. Language switcher: strip `base` and the current locale segment from Astro.url.pathname, then call getRelativeLocaleUrl(targetLocale, restOfPath) for each locale.
