If the target translation is missing (checked against the build-time translation map), disable the link or point it to that locale's subject index with a 'not translated yet' note. Never link to a 404.
findings.rationale: The Astro i18n docs do not mention emitting hreflang automatically, and astro:i18n has no helper that converts the current path to another locale. getRelativeLocaleUrl(locale, path?, options?) needs the path passed in explicitly and throws on an unknown locale. Google's rules: hreflang needs language codes with an optional region (zh-TW is valid, zh-Hant is also allowed), each version must list itself and all others, return links are required (one-way tags are ignored), URLs must be fully qualified, and x-default is the fallback, most useful on language selectors. Community write-ups confirm the reciprocity pitfall when a page exists in only one language.
findings.license_or_terms: @astrojs/sitemap: part of Astro (MIT, not re-verified)

findings.area: 2a. Math in MDX: remark-math + rehype-katex (build-time KaTeX) with mhchem
findings.recommendation: Default choice: remark-math 6.0.0 + rehype-katex 7.0.1 inside unified(), so formulas are rendered at build time and pages need no math JS. Pin one KaTeX version. rehype-katex@7.0.1 depends on katex ^0.16.0, so it resolves to a 0.16.x release, not the newest 0.19.1. Install the same katex 0.16.x at top level so npm dedupes to a single instance. Self-host katex/dist/katex.min.css and its fonts from that same installed version, because a CDN CSS of another version will not match. For chemistry, add `import 'katex/contrib/mhchem'` (an exported subpath in katex 0.16.x) before the rehype plugins run. That gives \ce{} and \pu{} for equations such as \ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}. Verify with a test build that it registers on the same katex instance rehype-katex uses. Fallback if it does not: write a roughly 30-line custom rehype plugin that calls katex@0.19.1 renderToString with mhchem loaded. For Chinese inside formulas, require authors to wrap it in \text{...}. Add CSS `.katex .cjk_fallback { font-family: 'Noto Sans TC', sans-serif; }`. Keep KaTeX `strict` at its 'warn' default so stray CJK in math mode shows up as build warnings. Keep `output` at its default 'htmlAndMathml', which adds hidden MathML for screen readers. Add a lint step that counts KaTeX warnings.
findings.rationale: KaTeX latest is 0.19.1 (Oct 2026, MIT). 0.19.0 changed `strict` callback semantics. rehype-katex 7.0.1 (MIT) pins katex ^0.16.0 and states that KaTeX output requires its CSS. The mhchem extension adds \ce and \pu. Its KaTeX adaptation is MIT, based on Apache-2.0 mhchem code by Martin Hensel and the MathJax Consortium. The KaTeX docs show only browser script-tag loading, but katex 0.16.x package.json exports ./contrib/mhchem as both .js and .mjs. KaTeX supported-functions docs: CJK glyphs are always accepted in text mode but come from system fonts. Fallback fonts are set via the .cjk_fallback class. Expect small vertical alignment issues, because KaTeX treats unknown glyphs as being as tall as the letter M.
findings.license_or_terms: KaTeX MIT; mhchem extension MIT (adaptation) over Apache-2.0 upstream; remark-math / rehype-katex MIT

findings.area: 2b. MathJax 4 / Temml alternatives and accessibility tradeoffs
findings.recommendation: Stay with build-time KaTeX for v1. Reconsider MathJax 4 (latest 4.1.3, Apache-2.0) only if interactive screen-reader exploration of formulas becomes a requirement. Its expression explorer is on by default and it generates speech, but it needs client-side JS on every math page. It also has built-in mhchem ([tex]/mhchem, autoloadable) and new line breaking for long formulas. rehype-mathjax (same remark-math monorepo) is the drop-in unified option. Temml (MIT; outputs MathML Core, minimal font about 10 KB, Latin Modern about 380 KB) via the third-party rehype-mathml is a lightweight MathML-only alternative. Its README notes Chromium rendering bugs with system fonts, so test on Chrome before choosing it.
findings.rationale: MathJax 4.0.0 shipped 2025-08-04, and 4.1.3 is the newest tagged release. The v4 notes cover extended fonts, display and inline line breaking, an updated Expression Explorer that is on by default, and speech-generation changes. MathJax-src is Apache-2.0. KaTeX's default htmlAndMathml already provides MathML for assistive tech with zero runtime JS, which fits a static course site better.
findings.license_or_terms: MathJax Apache-2.0; Temml MIT; rehype-mathjax MIT

findings.area: 3a. PhET simulations (physics and chemistry)
findings.recommendation: Use PhET only as optional supplementary embeds. Use the official Embed code from each sim page, inside a lazy-loaded iframe wrapper component. Place the required attribution next to each embed: 'Simulation by PhET Interactive Simulations, University of Colorado Boulder' + license + https://phet.colorado.edu. Do not hide or overlay the PhET logo. Keep the site strictly non-commercial: no ads, no paid tier, no sponsorship. Otherwise get a PhET commercial license (phet-partnerships@colorado.edu). Build the core explanations with the site's own widgets, so the course does not depend on a third-party license.
findings.rationale: PhET relicensed its whole sim library from CC BY to Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial (blog post 2026-03-30). Any use that gives commercial advantage or monetary compensation needs a commercial license, even for non-profits. Sims published before 2026-03-29 remain CC BY 4.0 ('Historical PhET Simulations'), and that agreement forbids modification other than translating the attribution. The PhET name and logo are trademarks, and the logo inside sims must stay visible and unaltered. School websites and course materials are listed as fine. The blog does not discuss iframes specifically.
findings.license_or_terms: Current library: CC BY-NC (version number not stated in the announcement). Pre-2026-03-29 versions: CC BY 4.0. Trademark restrictions on name/logo; commercial use needs a partnership agreement.

findings.area: 3b. GeoGebra embedding
findings.recommendation: Use GeoGebra only if the site stays non-commercial, and show 'Made with GeoGebra®' with a link to geogebra.org beside each embed. Prefer your own MIT/ISC-licensed widgets (see 3d/3e) for core content. Before embedding at scale or self-hosting the apps bundle, ask office@geogebra.org in writing, because the license pages do not address embedding or self-hosting.
findings.rationale: The GeoGebra license (last updated Nov 2025) allows free non-commercial copying, distribution and transmission, with attribution required for Materials. Commercial use needs a separate agreement, and its examples include using GeoGebra to secure advertising or sponsorship revenue. Language files and docs are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Source code is EUPL v1.2, but using it with the Materials as the GeoGebra product stays non-commercial only. The FAQ does not address embedding on websites or self-hosting.
findings.license_or_terms: GeoGebra Non-Commercial License Agreement (updated Nov 2025); CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for language/docs; EUPL-1.2 source

findings.area: 3c. Desmos API
findings.recommendation: Do not build widgets on the Desmos API unless you sign a paid plan or Commercial Addendum. A free public student-facing site appears to fall outside the free Trial Tier. Use JSXGraph or Mafs instead (see 3d).
findings.rationale: Desmos API Terms v1.0 (last updated 2025-07-11) limit the free Trial Tier to personal non-commercial use or a 90-day internal trial. Commercial use is defined to include any API use in an Application that end users access in production, and the terms contain no non-profit exception. An API key is required (v1.12 documented, with yearly April releases), and the generic demo key was deprecated. Branding must not be removed or obscured. This is a plain reading of the terms, not legal advice.
findings.license_or_terms: Proprietary; Trial Tier personal/non-commercial or 90-day evaluation only; production use requires paid plan/Commercial Addendum

findings.area: 3d. Interactive math and geometry widgets (self-built)
findings.recommendation: Build React widgets with Mafs (MIT, React components for interactive math) for coordinate planes, function graphs, vectors and draggable points. Use JSXGraph 1.14.3 (dual LGPL-3.0+/MIT, you can choose MIT) for richer dynamic geometry: constructions, sliders, conics, and probability visuals. Treat function-plot (MIT, built on D3) as optional, because its maintenance status could not be confirmed. Wrap each widget in an Astro island (client:visible) and take all labels from the locale dictionary.
findings.rationale: Licenses were verified on each repo. JSXGraph's README states the LGPL-or-MIT dual license, and its latest npm tag is 1.14.3. Mafs is MIT with tests and CI, but no latest version was shown. function-plot is MIT (copyright notice 2015-2023), and its last commit date could not be read.
findings.license_or_terms: Mafs MIT; JSXGraph LGPL-3.0-or-later OR MIT; function-plot MIT

findings.area: 3e. Data visualization (geography, civics, statistics)
findings.recommendation: Use Observable Plot 0.6.19 (ISC) for most charts: population pyramids, climographs, statistics distributions, economics curves. Drop down to D3 7.9.2 (ISC) for custom or animated diagrams and d3-geo maps. Render static charts at build time where possible, and hydrate only the interactive ones.
findings.rationale: Both are ISC-licensed per their GitHub repos. Latest npm tags were confirmed via jsDelivr.
findings.license_or_terms: ISC (both)

findings.area: 3f. Molecule viewer (chemistry / biology)
findings.recommendation: Use 3Dmol.js 2.5.5 (BSD license) via npm inside a React island for 3D molecular shapes such as VSEPR geometries, organic molecules and protein or DNA structures. Ship small local SDF/XYZ/PDB/CIF files instead of fetching from external databases. Credit the project and cite its Bioinformatics paper (DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btu829) on a credits page, as the authors request.
findings.rationale: The README says 3Dmol.js is under 'the permissive BSD open-source license'. The exact clause variant was not shown. Supported formats include pdb, sdf, mol2, xyz, cif and others. The latest npm tag is 2.5.5.
findings.license_or_terms: BSD (variant not confirmed on page); citation requested

findings.area: 4a. Map rendering libraries
findings.recommendation: Use MapLibre GL JS 6.18.0 (BSD-3-Clause) for interactive thematic maps with GeoJSON sources (Taiwan counties and townships, world regions, climate zones). Keep localIdeographFontFamily at its default 'sans-serif', or set it to your TC font stack, so Chinese labels render locally instead of downloading huge CJK glyph PBFs. Use Leaflet 1.9.4 (BSD-2-Clause, about 40 kB gzip) only for simple raster-tile maps. Leaflet 2.0 is still beta (2.0.0-beta.4). For static figures, prefer build-time SVG via d3-geo.
findings.rationale: MapLibre's README states the 3-Clause BSD license, and its latest npm tag is 6.18.0. localIdeographFontFamily defaults to 'sans-serif' and exists to avoid bandwidth-heavy glyph-server requests for CJK. Leaflet's repo lists BSD-2-Clause. jsDelivr tags: latest 1.9.4, beta 2.0.0-beta.4.
findings.license_or_terms: MapLibre GL JS BSD-3-Clause; Leaflet BSD-2-Clause

findings.area: 4b. Map data and basemaps (Natural Earth, Taiwan open data, tiles)
findings.recommendation: World layers: Natural Earth (public domain). For Taiwan-related boundaries, decide editorially between the default de facto layers and the Taiwan point-of-view file ne_10m_admin_0_countries_twn (v5.1.1), and say on the site which one you use. Taiwan layers: 內政部國土測繪中心 datasets on data.gov.tw: 鄉鎮市區界線(TWD97經緯度) (data.gov.tw/dataset/7441, SHP) and 直轄市、縣市界線(TWD97經緯度) (data.gov.tw/dataset/7442, SHP/GML). Convert and simplify them to TopoJSON/GeoJSON at build time. Both are under 政府資料開放授權條款-第1版, which requires an attribution line: agency, year, dataset name and version, a license statement, and the link https://data.gov.tw/license. Basemap tiles are optional for this course. If needed, self-host a Taiwan-region PMTiles extract (Protomaps; OSM data under ODbL, attribution required). OpenFreeMap (MIT, free, no key, but no SLA) is the zero-setup option. Do not depend on tile.openstreetmap.org: it is best-effort with no SLA and may block heavy use without warning.
findings.rationale: Natural Earth: public domain, credit optional, commercial use allowed. Its policy draws de facto boundaries by default and offers 33 POV downloads including twn. The Taiwan open-data license (enacted 2015-07-27) allows any use, including derivatives, and is compatible with CC BY 4.0. Without the attribution, the license treats the rights as never granted. Dataset metadata was updated 2025-12-24 (7441) and 2025-12-16 (7442). OSMF tile policy: attribution, valid Referer, and caching are required. Bulk or offline use is prohibited, and there is no SLA.
findings.license_or_terms: Natural Earth public domain; 政府資料開放授權條款第1版 (CC BY 4.0-compatible, attribution mandatory); OSM data ODbL; OpenFreeMap MIT

findings.area: 5. Search over bilingual CJK content
findings.recommendation: Use Pagefind 1.6.0 (MIT) as a post-build step (`astro build && pagefind --site dist`, as in the reference project). Set <html lang="zh-TW"> on Chinese pages and lang="en" on English pages. zh-tw is one of the three codes Pagefind documents for Chinese segmentation. Pagefind builds separate per-language indexes and searches only the current page's language. Put data-pagefind-body on <main>, and data-pagefind-ignore on navigation, quiz answer keys and repeated dialogue speaker labels. Use data-pagefind-filter for subject (數學/物理/化學/生物/歷史/地理/公民/國文). Put the English term in parentheses on zh pages, e.g. 導數 (derivative), so learners can find terms in either script. Use the new Component UI (1.5+), whose 1.6.0 release fixed IME composition keystrokes, which matters for 注音/倉頡 typing. Alternative only if you need custom ranking: Orama (core Apache-2.0) with @orama/tokenizers/mandarin. The license of the tokenizer package itself is unverified.
findings.rationale: Pagefind segments unspaced Chinese on pages tagged zh, zh-cn or zh-tw. This needs the extended release, which npx pagefind uses by default. Chinese gets no stemming. v1.6.0 (2026-11-01) segments Chinese at index time with ICU4X, aligned with the browser's Intl.Segmenter used for queries. v1.5.0 added query-side segmentation, improved zh-TW UI translations, and introduced the Component UI. Pagefind skips nav and footer by default, and data-pagefind-body limits indexing to the marked region.
findings.license_or_terms: Pagefind MIT; Orama core Apache-2.0 (tokenizer package license unverified)

findings.area: 6a. Traditional Chinese web fonts: choice, licensing, subsetting
findings.recommendation: Body text: Noto Sans TC (OFL-1.1). The Noto CJK 'TC' region subset is the Taiwan glyph set, and Taiwan centers its punctuation. Self-host it with Fontsource (@fontsource/noto-sans-tc, or the variable 100-900 build), which ships about 100+ unicode-range woff2 slices per weight, so browsers download only the slices a page uses. Load at most 2 weights (400/700), and preload only the Latin face. Optional serif for headings or history quotes: Noto Serif TC (same family and approach). For the professor/student dialogue voice, a friendlier face is possible. LXGW WenKai TC (OFL-1.1, also on Fontsource with sliced CSS) uses 傳承字形, not the 教育部國字標準字體 forms that Taiwanese students learn. Its README itself points to 芫荽 Iansui (OFL-1.1, v1.020 beta, loosely follows MOE standard forms) for Taiwan-standard shapes. Prefer Iansui for the dialogue voice, or keep everything in Noto TC. Use LXGW WenKai TC only after an explicit editorial decision, and never for 國文 content where character forms matter. Do not hotlink Google Fonts. Self-hosting avoids third-party requests, and Google's CSS response varies by client.
findings.rationale: The Noto CJK Sans README labels TC as Taiwan (臺灣) Traditional Chinese, with 7 static weights plus variable builds, release Sans2.004. The Noto CJK LICENSE file is SIL OFL 1.1. The Fontsource CSS for Noto Sans TC and for LXGW WenKai TC both contain 96+ @font-face blocks, each with a unicode-range. LXGW WenKai TC is OFL 1.1, and its README says it follows inherited forms (傳承字形) and recommends Iansui for Taiwan standard forms. Iansui is OFL 1.1 and aims to approximate MOE standard forms, with loose rules.
findings.license_or_terms: Noto Sans/Serif TC: SIL OFL 1.1; LXGW WenKai TC: SIL OFL 1.1; Iansui: SIL OFL 1.1 (all allow web embedding/redistribution; fonts may not be sold alone)

findings.area: 6b. Traditional Chinese typography CSS: punctuation, CJK-Latin spacing, line height
findings.recommendation: Set <html lang="zh-TW"> and a TC-first font stack, so punctuation sits centered in the character box as Taiwan convention expects. Do not let SC fonts win the fallback order. Authoring convention: type full-width punctuation (，。、；：「」『』？！) in zh text, and do not hand-insert spaces between Han and Latin or digits. Apply `text-autospace: normal` as progressive enhancement. Chrome/Edge 140+, Firefox 145+ and Safari 18.4+ support it (Baseline 2025), and it adds about 1/4-em CJK-Latin spacing in the layout engine. Add `text-spacing-trim: normal` only as an enhancement: Chrome/Edge 123+ only, and it needs fonts with the halt/chws OpenType features. Line height: clreq gives no single body-text ratio. Pick it by visual testing of mixed zh/en/math paragraphs. Add extra line gap wherever ruby/注音 annotations appear.
findings.rationale: W3C clreq (Group Note Draft dated 2026-11-04): Taiwan and Hong Kong usually center punctuation in its square, while mainland China places it toward a corner. The Han-Western gap is in principle no more than a quarter of a Han character width, nothing is added at line start or end, and justification may vary it between 1/8 and 1/2 em. Line-gap minimums are given only for interlinear marks (at least half the font size) and vertical bopomofo (more than 1.5x). MDN browser-compat-data gives the support versions above. Implementations use no-autospace as the initial value, so the property must be set explicitly. text-spacing-trim is not supported in Firefox or Safari.
findings.license_or_terms: n/a

findings.area: 6c. Ruby / 注音 (bopomofo) support
findings.recommendation: For occasional pronunciations (rare characters and 破音字 in history, geography or the 國文 beta), use semantic <ruby>字<rt>ㄗˋ</rt></ruby> with ruby-position: over, or an inline parenthetical 注音. Ruby over/under works in Chrome/Edge 84+, Firefox 38+ and Safari 18.2+. Do not rely on `ruby-position: inter-character`, the traditional right-side bopomofo placement. Chrome and Firefox do not implement it, and Safari 18.2's implementation is partial: tone marks are mispositioned. If full right-side 注音 is ever needed (likely only for the 國文 beta), evaluate ButTaiwan's bpmfvs 注音 fonts. They render zhuyin from the font itself and pick 破音字 readings with IVS selectors, so readings survive copy-paste. Their license wording and web file sizes must be checked first.
findings.rationale: MDN BCD: inter-character is 'not implemented' in Chrome, Edge and Firefox, and partial in Safari 18.2 because bopomofo tone marks are not positioned correctly. MDN says inter-character is intended for bopomofo. clreq: bopomofo normally sits to the right of the base character, at about a 3:10 size ratio, with tone-mark placement rules. bpmfvs: one font file handles polyphonic characters via IVS, and GSUB stylistic sets are a fallback. The project code is Apache-2.0, and the fonts are described as under an 'OTF 1.1' license, presumably meaning OFL 1.1 (unconfirmed).
findings.license_or_terms: bpmfvs code Apache-2.0; fonts stated as 'OTF 1.1' (likely OFL 1.1, unconfirmed)

findings.area: 7. Static hosting
findings.recommendation: Primary: Cloudflare, either Pages or Workers Static Assets with no Worker script. Static-asset requests are free and unlimited on Workers, and Pages Free lists no bandwidth cap. Watch the 20,000-file limit on both free tiers: CJK font slices (about 100+ per weight per family) plus Pagefind fragments add up, so count files in dist/ in CI. Pages Free: 500 builds/month, 1 concurrent, 20-min build timeout, 25 MiB per file. Good free alternative: GitHub Pages via withastro/action v6. Limits: 1 GB published site, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10-minute deploy timeout, not allowed as hosting for an online business. Set `site` and, for a project page, `base:'/repo'`, which every internal link (including locale links) must carry. Avoid Netlify Free for an actively edited course. Its 300-credit monthly hard cap (15 credits per production deploy, 20 credits per GB of bandwidth) pauses all of the team's projects until the next cycle once used up. Whatever the host, match trailingSlash to build.format ('always' with the default 'directory').
findings.rationale: Cloudflare docs: static asset requests on Workers are free and unlimited. Free allows 20,000 files per version (100,000 paid), 25 MiB per file. Pages Free limits are as listed. The migration guide says Workers support _headers/_redirects natively and claims general parity, but it does not deprecate Pages. GitHub Pages limits come from GitHub docs. Netlify: 300 credits/month hard limit on Free with no auto-recharge, and paused projects show 'Site not available'. Astro config reference: trailingSlash defaults to 'ignore' and the host decides for prerendered pages, and build.format defaults to 'directory'.
findings.license_or_terms: Cloudflare/GitHub/Netlify ToS; GitHub Pages prohibits use as free hosting for an online business

open_questions: Astro i18n custom locale paths (the { path, codes } object form): the docs' Limitations section seems to require output:'server' with no prerendered pages, but the wording may refer only to the domains feature. A static test build is needed before using the object form. Plain string codes ('zh-tw', 'en') are safe.
Does Astro's getRelativeLocaleUrl() automatically prepend `base`? This matters for GitHub project pages. Not confirmed in the docs that were read; test it.
Pagefind documents Chinese segmentation for lang 'zh', 'zh-cn' and 'zh-tw' only. Whether 'zh-Hant' or 'zh-Hant-TW' also trigger segmentation is unverified, so use lang='zh-TW' unless tested.

mhchem with rehype-katex in Astro 7's unified pipeline: does `import 'katex/contrib/mhchem'` in astro.config.mjs register \ce on the same katex instance rehype-katex uses? This needs a test build. The fallback is a custom rehype plugin calling katex directly.
Is there a rehype-katex release that accepts KaTeX 0.17+? The current 7.0.1 pins katex ^0.16.0, while KaTeX latest is 0.19.1.
remark-math inside MDX: check that LaTeX braces {} in $...$ are not parsed as JSX expressions under @astrojs/mdx 8 + unified(). Not verified this session.

PhET: what exactly counts as 'commercial' for a free, ad-free public site run by an individual? How many target sims have zh_TW translations (the zh_TW browse page did not show translated titles)? Which sims are post-2026-03-29 (CC BY-NC) vs historical (CC BY 4.0)?
GeoGebra: the license and FAQ pages do not address iframe embedding or self-hosting the apps bundle on a free educational site. This needs written confirmation from office@geogebra.org.
國土測繪中心 (NLSC) 通用版電子地圖 WMTS (EMAP5_OPENDATA): official terms for embedding tiles in a public website were not found.
Do Noto Sans TC glyph shapes conform to 教育部國字標準字體? The README only confirms 'TC = Taiwan' region glyphs. Iansui follows MOE forms loosely. LXGW WenKai TC uses 傳承字形.

Does Astro's Fonts API (fontsource/google providers) preserve the 100+ unicode-range slices for CJK fonts, or download whole files? Undocumented, so test before relying on it. Otherwise import @fontsource CSS directly.
Google Fonts CSS2 for Noto Sans TC returned unsliced TTF to the fetch client. Slicing behavior for real browsers was not verified (moot if self-hosting).

Cloudflare Workers Free: does the 100,000 requests/day limit count requests served purely from static assets? The billing page says static asset requests are free and unlimited, while the limits page phrases the cap per Worker request.
bpmfvs 注音 fonts: confirm the license (stated as 'OTF 1.1') and measure woff2 sizes for web delivery.
Natural Earth: decide editorially between default (de facto) and Taiwan-POV (twn) admin-0 layers for maps shown to Taiwanese students, especially for 地理 and 歷史 content.
Out of scope for this platform topic and not researched: the 116學年度學測 date and 測驗範圍 from 大考中心 (another workflow step should confirm these).

WebSearch budget ran out midway through this research. Remaining facts were verified only via direct WebFetch of the cited primary pages. Topics that would have needed new discovery searches (e.g., other CJK search engines, MOE-standard font comparisons) were not explored further.

verification.topic: Fact-check of the 'Web platform & licenses' research report (Astro i18n, KaTeX/mhchem, PhET/GeoGebra/Desmos, viz/map libraries, data.gov.tw licensing, Pagefind CJK, TC fonts and typography, static hosting). Checked 2026-11-15 by opening primary pages directly.

confirmed.claim: Astro 7.0 came out 2026-06-22 and made Sätteri the default Markdown/MDX processor. remark/rehype plugins need @astrojs/markdown-remark with markdown.processor: unified({...}). @astrojs/markdown-remark is no longer installed by default.
In Astro 7.0, compressHTML's default changed from true to 'jsx'. Example from the guide: helloworld renders as 'helloworld'. The fix is {" "}, or set compressHTML: true.
unified() is imported from @astrojs/markdown-remark and is 'a unified-based processor to render .md and .mdx files'.

Sätteri only parses math (opt-in) and has no native KaTeX rendering. It runs no remark/rehype plugins unmodified. This comes from a third-party blog. The official Sätteri and Markdown docs pages do not mention math at all.
satteri-plugins is a community monorepo (MIT, about 12 stars) that includes satteri-katex. Its first releases are 0.1.0.

Astro 6 requires Node 22.12.0 or higher, upgrades to Zod 4 (import { z } from 'astro/zod'), and moves collection config to src/content.config.ts. In Astro 6.0, redirectToDefaultLocale defaults to false and only works with prefixDefaultLocale: true.

Astro i18n: prefixDefaultLocale defaults to false. With true, unprefixed URLs return 404 unless a fallback is set. fallbackType was added in 4.15.0. domains needs server output with the @astrojs/node or @astrojs/vercel adapter. Folder names must match locales exactly. hreflang is not mentioned on the page.
Astro 6.1 (2026-03-26) automatically includes i18n fallback pages in the generated sitemap.
The @astrojs/sitemap docs show v3.7.5. The i18n option takes defaultLocale plus a locales key-to-lang map and emits xhtml:link alternates.
getRelativeLocaleUrl(locale, path?, options?) throws on an unknown locale. No helper converts the current path to another locale. The docs do not say whether base is prepended.
The glob() loader's default IDs use github-slugger. generateId is a callback, and the docs say nothing about non-ASCII filenames. deferRender was added in astro@7.1.0.
The i18n recipe uses src/content/<collection>/<lang>/ folders and a ui.ts/t() helper. Missing keys silently fall back to the default language.
Astro config defaults: trailingSlash is 'ignore', and the hosting platform handles trailing slashes on prerendered pages. build.format is 'directory'. compressHTML is 'jsx'.

Reference project (read-only): astro ^7.4.12, @astrojs/mdx ^8.1.6, @astrojs/react ^7.1.9, react ^19.3.1, pagefind ^1.6.0. The build script is 'astro build && pagefind --site dist'. The config uses processor: unified({ remarkPlugins: [[remarkDialogue, { base }]] }). It also pins @astrojs/markdown-remark ^7.3.9, which the report did not list.
Astro is MIT licensed.
KaTeX v0.19.1 is the latest (2026-10-23). 0.19.0's breaking changes: missing metrics are reported via strict (symbolNotInFont), and strict callbacks returning undefined/null now warn.
rehype-katex is 7.0.1 (MIT) with katex ^0.16.0. remark-math is 6.0.0 (MIT). The highest katex 0.16.x on npm is 0.16.47, which is what ^0.16.0 resolves to today.
katex 0.16.x package.json exports ./contrib/mhchem as require ./dist/contrib/mhchem.js and import ./dist/contrib/mhchem.mjs.

mhchem adds \ce and \pu, and its README shows only <script> loading. The file header: (c) 2011-2015 MathJax Consortium and (c) 2015-2018 Martin Hensel under Apache 2.0, with the KaTeX adaptation released under MIT.

KaTeX defaults are output 'htmlAndMathml' (MathML for accessibility) and strict 'warn'. CJK glyphs are always accepted in text mode but come from system fonts. A .cjk_fallback class is available. Unknown glyphs are treated as tall as 'M'.

MathJax-src's latest release is v4.1.3, and v4.0.0 was released 04 Aug. The v4 notes cover extended fonts, display and inline line breaking, and an Expression Explorer that is on by default. mhchem is autoloaded.

Temml is MIT and outputs MathML Core, with a minimal font of about 10 KB and Latin Modern at about 380 KB. Its README says 'Chromium has some rendering bugs when using system fonts'. rehype-mathml (@daiji256/rehype-mathml, MIT, uses temml) is third-party, and the remark-math README lists it. rehype-mathjax is in the remark-math monorepo.

PhET blog post dated 2026-03-30: the entire library moves from CC BY to CC BY-NC. Uses giving 'commercial advantage or monetary compensation' need a license, including by non-profits. Classrooms, assignments, course materials and school websites are OK. The post names no license version.

Sims published before March 29, 2026 ('Historical PhET Simulations') are CC BY 4.0. Required attribution: 'Simulation by PhET Interactive Simulations, University of Colorado Boulder, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://phet.colorado.edu)'. The logo must stay visible, unobstructed and unaltered.

GeoGebra license, last updated November 2025: non-commercial use, copying, distribution, modification and transmission of Materials are allowed. Attribution means name, copyright notice ('Made with GeoGebra®') and a link. Securing advertising or sponsorship revenue counts as commercial. Language files and docs are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Source code is EUPL v1.2, but use together with the Materials stays non-commercial. Contact: office@geogebra.org. The page does not mention embedding.

Desmos API Terms Version 1.0 (updated July 11, 2025): the Trial Tier is personal non-commercial use or a 90-day internal trial. 'Commercial use includes any use of the API in an Application that is accessed by End Users in production.' There is no non-profit exception. Branding must not be removed. Going beyond the Trial Tier means self-service or a Commercial Addendum (partnerships@desmos.com).
The Desmos API docs are v1.12 and an API key is required. Stable versions come out once per year in April.

JSXGraph is dual LGPL (v3 or later) or MIT, and its npm latest is 1.14.3. Mafs is MIT ('React components for interactive math'), with no version shown. function-plot is MIT (2015-2023), built on D3, with no last-commit date visible.
npm latest tags: @observablehq/plot 0.6.19 (ISC), d3 7.9.2 (ISC), 3dmol 2.5.5, maplibre-gl 6.18.0, leaflet 1.9.4 (beta 2.0.0-beta.4).
3Dmol.js uses 'the permissive BSD open-source license' (variant not stated). Formats include pdb, sdf, mol2, xyz and cif. Users are asked to cite DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btu829.

MapLibre GL JS is 3-Clause BSD. localIdeographFontFamily defaults to 'sans-serif' and exists 'to avoid bandwidth-intensive glyph server requests'. Leaflet is BSD-2-Clause, about 40 kB gzipped JS plus 2.4 kB CSS.

Natural Earth is public domain, credit is unnecessary, and commercial use is allowed. Default boundaries are de facto, with optional de jure POV downloads, including a Taiwan POV file ne_10m_admin_0_countries_twn.zip in version 5.1.1.

政府資料開放授權條款－第1版 was enacted 中華民國104年7月27日. It grants broad rights including derivatives. Attribution covers agency, year, dataset name and version, a license statement and a link. Without it, '視為自始未取得開放資料之授權' (the license counts as never granted). It is compatible with CC BY 4.0.
data.gov.tw/dataset/7441 is 鄉鎮市區界線(TWD97經緯度) from 內政部國土測繪中心: SHP, 政府資料開放授權條款-第1版, metadata updated 2025-12-24. Dataset 7442 is 直轄市、縣市界線(TWD97經緯度): SHP and GML, same license, updated 2025-12-16.

OSMF tile policy: best-effort with no SLA, access may be blocked without notice. Attribution, a valid Referer and honoring cache headers are required. Offline and bulk use is prohibited. OpenFreeMap is MIT, free, needs no API keys and has no SLA. Protomaps basemaps are ODbL and require OSM attribution, with region cutouts via pmtiles extract.

Pagefind segments Chinese on pages tagged zh, zh-cn or zh-tw. This needs the extended release, which npx pagefind uses by default. Specialized languages get no stemming. Indexes are built separately per language, and search covers only the current page's language. Pagefind is MIT.

Pagefind v1.6.0 (01 Nov) moved to ICU4X segmentation, closer to the browser's Intl.Segmenter, and fixed IME composition keystrokes. v1.5.0 (06 Apr) added query-side CJK segmentation via Intl.Segmenter, improved zh-TW translations, and introduced the Component UI, which replaces the Default UI.
Pagefind does not index <nav> and <footer> by default. data-pagefind-body limits indexing to the marked regions.
Noto CJK Sans: TC is the Taiwan Traditional Chinese subset, with 7 weights plus variable builds, released as Sans2.004. The license is SIL OFL 1.1.
LXGW WenKai TC is OFL 1.1, follows 傳承字形, and points users to 芫荽 Iansui for 臺灣教育標準字形. Iansui is OFL 1.1, version 1.020, still Beta, and adjusts glyphs '盡可能' toward 教育部標準字體 with a loose interpretation.
The Fontsource Noto Sans TC (variable 100-900, OFL-1.1) and LXGW WenKai TC 400.css files each have 95+ visible @font-face blocks, each with unicode-range.

clreq Group Note Draft dated 04 November 2026. Taiwan and Hong Kong center punctuation. Han-Western spacing is up to 1/4 em except at line start or end, adjustable from 1/8 em down to 1/2 em up. Single-sided interlinear marks need a line gap of at least half the font size (5/8 when double-sided). Bopomofo sits to the right at a 3:10 size ratio, and vertical bopomofo needs more than 1.5x line gap. There is no body line-height recommendation.

text-autospace is supported in Chrome/Edge 140, Firefox 145 and Safari 18.4, with initial value no-autospace in implementations. MDN marks it Baseline 2025 (since November 2025). text-spacing-trim works in Chrome/Edge 123 only, not in Firefox or Safari.

ruby-position over/under is supported in Chrome/Edge 84, Firefox 38 and Safari 18.2. inter-character is not supported in Chrome, Edge or Firefox, and is partial in Safari 18.2 (bopomofo tone marks are mispositioned). MDN says inter-character 'is intended for bopomofo (zhuyin fuhao) ruby'.
bpmfvs code is Apache 2.0. It picks 破音字 readings with IVS selectors that survive copy-paste, with a GSUB stylistic-set fallback, and IVS is still recommended. The fonts are stated as 'OTF 1.1授權'.

Google hreflang rules: ISO 639-1 language plus optional region. Scripts such as zh-Hant are allowed. Each version must list itself and all others. Non-reciprocal tags are ignored. URLs must be fully qualified. x-default was 'designed for language selector pages'. Google also advises separate URLs per language, no automatic language redirects, language-switch links, and translating the main content, not just the template.
A dev.to article ('Reciprocal hreflang in Astro, only when both languages exist') describes the one-language-entry reciprocity pitfall.

Cloudflare Pages Free: 500 builds/month, 1 concurrent, 20-minute timeout, 20,000 files, 25 MiB per file, no bandwidth cap listed. Workers static asset requests are 'free and unlimited'. Workers allows 20,000 files per version on Free and 100,000 on Paid, 25 MiB per file. The migration guide says Workers support _headers/_redirects natively, claims parity with exceptions, and does not deprecate Pages.

GitHub Pages: 1 GB per site, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10-minute deploy timeout, not allowed as free hosting for an online business. Astro's deploy guide uses withastro/action@v6 and says to set base to '/repo-name' for project pages.

Netlify Free: 300 credits/month with a hard limit and no recharge. A production deploy costs 15 credits, and 1 GB of bandwidth costs 20 credits. When the limit is hit, all of the team's projects pause and show 'Site not available' until the next billing cycle.

corrections.original: 6b: `text-autospace: normal` ... adds about 1/4-em CJK-Latin spacing in the layout engine.
corrections.correction: CSS Text Level 4 says the autospace keywords insert 1/8 of the CJK advance measure (0.125ic), not 1/4 em. The 1/4 em figure is clreq's upper bound for manually set Han-Western spacing, not what the CSS property inserts. Also, Chrome/Edge 140 support only the normal and no-autospace values. auto, ideograph-alpha, ideograph-numeric and insert have no Chrome version (Safari added insert only in v27).

corrections.original: 1b: deferRender (Astro 7.1) can postpone Markdown rendering until a page needs it.
corrections.correction: The loader reference says deferRender (astro@7.1.0, default false) does not apply to MDX, Markdoc or data entries. The report recommends .mdx lesson files, so deferRender would do nothing for that collection. It only helps plain .md entries, and when on, rendered HTML is no longer cached.

corrections.original: 3a: Sims published before 2026-03-29 remain CC BY 4.0 ('Historical PhET Simulations'), and that agreement forbids modification other than translating the attribution.
corrections.correction: The only modification rule on the page is about the attribution text: 'Translations of the attribution text are permitted, other modifications are not permitted.' The page does not say the simulations themselves may not be modified. The report's wording overstates the rule. The required attribution for historical sims also ends with 'licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://phet.colorado.edu)'. The historical-sims page explicitly does not cover sims published after that date.

corrections.original: 3b: Source code is EUPL v1.2 ... The FAQ does not address embedding on websites or self-hosting. (cites https://www.geogebra.org/license/faq)
corrections.correction: EUPL v1.2 is correct per the current /license page (updated Nov 2025), which also carries a FAQ saying EUPL 1.2. But the separate /license/faq URL the report cites is a stale page: guidelines May 2014, terms April 2013, FAQ January 2015. It still says source code is 'GNU General Public License (version 3 or later)'. Do not quote /license/faq as current. The point that neither page covers iframe embedding or self-hosting holds for both.

corrections.original: 6c: bpmfvs fonts are described as under an 'OTF 1.1' license, presumably meaning OFL 1.1 (unconfirmed).
corrections.correction: The README says '隨本規格發佈的注音字型，目前已一律統一為OTF 1.1授權' and defers to each font's bundled documentation. It also says derived fonts may use other license terms and be sold commercially if the original NOTICE.txt copyright info is kept. That does not match OFL 1.1, which requires modified versions to stay under OFL, and the NOTICE.txt requirement looks more like Apache-2.0. The 'presumably OFL 1.1' guess is unsupported. Read the bundled license file before use.

corrections.original: 2a: rehype-katex@7.0.1 depends on katex ^0.16.0, so it resolves to a 0.16.x release.
corrections.correction: This is correct but can be made exact: the highest 0.16.x on npm today is 0.16.47, so ^0.16.0 resolves there. Pin top-level katex to the same 0.16.47 and self-host its CSS and fonts. The report cites the v0.16.22 package.json for the mhchem export. That entry is very likely unchanged in 0.16.47, but it was not re-checked.

corrections.original: 6a: Fontsource ships about 100+ unicode-range woff2 slices per weight.
corrections.correction: In the Noto Sans TC 400.css, slice indexes run at least to [115], so over 116 slices per weight. Each @font-face also references a .woff fallback next to the .woff2. If the bundler emits both, the dist/ file count roughly doubles per weight. That matters for the 20,000-file free-tier limits in section 7.

corrections.original: 4b: Natural Earth ... offers 33 POV downloads including twn.
corrections.correction: The page does not state a count. The 33 download links include ISO and top-level-countries variants, so 33 is a link count, not necessarily 33 distinct points of view. The Taiwan POV file and version 5.1.1 are confirmed.

unverifiable.claim: The Astro i18n Limitations (site mandatory, output 'server', no prerendered pages) apply to custom { path, codes } locales, as opposed to only the domains feature.
unverifiable.reason: The fetched page text puts '#### Limitations' under 'Custom locale paths'. But the same block requires forwarded host/protocol headers, which only make sense for domains, so the page-to-markdown conversion may have misplaced it. The report's open question stands. Plain string locales are safe either way.

unverifiable.claim: getRelativeLocaleUrl() automatically prepends `base`.
unverifiable.reason: The astro:i18n reference only lists base among settings to 'take into account' and does not say. A test build is needed.

unverifiable.claim: PhET commercial licenses are handled at phet-partnerships@colorado.edu.
unverifiable.reason: Neither the blog post, the licensing pages nor the /en/partnerships page fetched shows this address. The licensing page's email is obfuscated, and /en/licensing returned no license text.

unverifiable.claim: The current PhET library is CC BY-NC (specific version).
unverifiable.reason: The announcement names no version, and the /en/licensing page content did not load. Treat it as 'CC BY-NC, version unconfirmed'.

unverifiable.claim: The generic Desmos demo API key was deprecated.
unverifiable.reason: Neither desmos.com/api nor the v1.12 docs mentions a demo key. They only say a key is required, available from desmos.com/my-api.

unverifiable.claim: MathJax 4.0.0 shipped 2025-08-04.
unverifiable.reason: The GitHub release list shows '04 Aug' without a year, and mathjax.org shows no date. The order (4.1.0 Dec, 4.1.1 Feb, 4.1.2 May, 4.1.3 Jul) fits 2025, but the year was not shown.

unverifiable.claim: Orama's Mandarin tokenizer is @orama/tokenizers/mandarin (core Apache-2.0).
unverifiable.reason: The Orama 'Using Chinese with Orama' page returned only navigation, not the article body.

unverifiable.claim: Workers Free's 100,000 requests/day cap does not count pure static-asset requests.
unverifiable.reason: The billing page says static asset requests are 'free and unlimited', but the limits page phrases the cap per Worker request and does not say whether asset-only requests count.

unverifiable.claim: Mafs has tests and CI.
unverifiable.reason: The GitHub page fetch showed only the MIT license, description and commit count. CI/test badges were not readable.

unverifiable.claim: Noto Sans TC glyphs conform to 教育部國字標準字體.
unverifiable.reason: The Noto README only says TC means Taiwan. The Iansui README says its loose interpretation of the MOE standard is '如同思源宋體、思源黑體、蘋方等其他字型', which suggests Source Han / Noto TC also follows MOE forms only loosely. That is a third party's statement, not an official Noto conformance claim.

unverifiable.claim: Pagefind treats lang='zh-TW' (uppercase region) and zh-Hant variants the same as 'zh-tw'.
unverifiable.reason: The docs list only lowercase zh, zh-cn and zh-tw. Case handling and script subtags are not documented, so this needs a test build.

unverifiable.claim: remark-math $...$ braces are safe from JSX parsing under @astrojs/mdx 8 + unified().
unverifiable.reason: The remark-math README does not mention MDX, and no Astro page fetched covers it. This needs a test build.

verification.notes:
Method: every check used WebFetch on primary pages. The one WebSearch attempt (for the PhET commercial license) came back 'budget used up', because the limit is shared across agents in this turn. So no Traditional Chinese discovery searches were run. The only zh-TW official sources involved (data.gov.tw license and datasets 7441/7442) were checked directly and match the report. For the reference project, only package.json and astro.config.mjs were read, read-only, with no writes.

Overall the report is accurate. Version numbers (Astro 7.4, KaTeX 0.19.1, rehype-katex 7.0.1, remark-math 6.0.0, MathJax 4.1.3, JSXGraph 1.14.3, Plot 0.6.19, D3 7.9.2, 3Dmol 2.5.5, MapLibre 6.18.0, Leaflet 1.9.4 / 2.0.0-beta.4, Pagefind 1.6.0, sitemap 3.7.5) all match jsDelivr, GitHub or the official docs. No invented licenses were found. The substantive errors are:
(1) text-autospace inserts 1/8 ic, not 1/4 em.
(2) deferRender does not apply to the MDX files the report recommends.
(3) The PhET 'forbids modification' wording is overstated.
(4) The cited GeoGebra /license/faq URL is a stale 2013-2015 page saying GPL.
(5) The bpmfvs 'likely OFL' inference is not supported by its own wording.

Additions the plan should take on:
(a) Pagefind: once any page uses data-pagefind-body, pages without it are excluded from the index. Every lesson layout, and any index or chooser page meant to be searchable, must carry it.
(b) Netlify also charges web requests, 2 credits per 10,000.
(c) Pagefind 1.5+ docs say the Component UI replaces the Default UI (pagefind-ui.js / PagefindUI), so the reference project's UI choice may need updating.
(d) The GitHub Pages soft limit of 10 builds/hour does not apply to custom Actions workflows such as withastro/action.

Out of scope here, as the report itself notes: 116學年度學測 scope and dates from 大考中心 were not checked by this platform report or by this fact-check.
